Name: Bruce Banman
Bio:
Bruce Banman is a dedicated public servant who has been representing the residents of Abbotsford South with unwavering commitment since his election as MLA in 2020. On September 13, 2023, Bruce joined the Conservative Party of British Columbia and was appointed House Leader.

A Longtime Resident and Advocate

A proud resident of Abbotsford since 1982, Bruce Banman’s roots run deep in the heart of Abbotsford South. His journey into politics was fueled by a genuine desire to better serve his community. Bruce’s extensive experience as a city councillor and as the mayor of Abbotsford has afforded him unique insights into the diverse needs and aspirations of his constituents.

Champion of Agricultural Issues and Affordable Housing

Throughout his career in public service, Bruce Banman has emerged as a steadfast advocate for critical issues facing Abbotsford South. His unwavering commitment to agricultural sustainability highlights his dedication to preserving the region’s rich farming heritage. Simultaneously, his tireless work in advocating for affordable housing solutions underscores his commitment to ensuring that all residents have access to safe and affordable housing.

A Multifaceted Career Path

Before venturing into the realm of politics, Bruce Banman carved out a successful career as a chiropractor and owned his own small business. This entrepreneurial spirit and business acumen have complemented his journey in public service, equipping him with the insights and practical knowledge necessary to navigate complex challenges.

Experience, Passion, and Vision

Bruce Banman’s leadership is defined by a harmonious fusion of experience, passion, and vision. His broad background uniquely positions him to advocate on behalf of Abbotsford South effectively. He understands the intricate dynamics of both the public and private sectors, enabling him to bridge gaps and drive positive change.

Name: Robin Roy
Bio:
Robin Roy, born in Weyburn, Saskatchewan, spent his childhood in Chilliwack and Abbotsford, attending Unsworth Elementary and Yale Junior High. His family then lived for almost 10 years in Victoria, and he has spent his adult life in Langley and now Abbotsford.

In Victoria, Robin began a construction company. He married and moved back to the mainland to open another construction company here. In 1998, Robin transitioned into a career in information technology and began a computer service company, which he operates today, working with clients in all sectors of business and life across the Lower Mainland.

Robin has been married for thirty-four years and has three adult children and one grandchild. Because of his passionate desire for an amazing future for his children and all the people of BC, he has chosen to stand and offer to serve in the provincial legislature and represent the people of Abbotsford South, where he resides.

Robin passionately believes that we live in the most beautiful place in the world and desires to work to keep our citizens safe and free to pursue their dreams.

Name: Korky Neufeld
Bio:
Korky Neufeld is an enthusiastic and hardworking individual with a diverse professional background in the political, religious, and industrial sectors. 

He was born into a family of 10 children. His parents emigrated from South America in 1964 with a dream of a better life for the future generations. Korky places significant value on family, his own including his wife of 40 years – Cynthia, four children and two grandchildren.

Professional Journey

Korky’s professional life has been marked by service.

He began his career in church ministry – first, as a pastor in Vancouver, then leading a church that served the people of Abbotsford for over a decade. Intermittently, Korky worked many years in the construction industry, grasping the challenges of blue-collar workers and families.

His current role as Construction Manager for Servicemaster Restore of the Fraser Valley brings him into city halls across the entire region, enabling him to work with municipal systems to help people who have undergone life-altering events.

Affecting Change in the Political Sphere

Korky spent 15 years as the Abbotsford Board of Education Trustee. In that time, he also served several years as the Chair and Vice-Chair, working closely with the Superintendent (the lead educator) and the Secretary Treasurer (the operational leader). These positions have allowed Korky to learn what it takes to affect important educational change on a systemic level.

One of Korky’s roles over the years on the Abbotsford School Board has been to represent Abbotsford at the British Columbia School Trustee Association. This provincial association is made up of sixty boards from all over the province, with over 350 elected trustees as its members. Korky was elected for two terms by his peers to represent them as one of seven directors on this provincial board. This leadership experience widened his knowledge, facilitating the opportunity to see beyond his district’s level into the needs of diverse regions across the province. It also allowed him to further build into his skill-set for best representing unique and complex issues.

Community Engagement (Prioritizing Serving People in the Community) 

Korky has served on multiple provincial and advisory committees, including:

Abbotsford Restorative Justice and Advocacy Association (5+ yrs) – advocating for restorative processes for first-time offenders

Bridgehouse Committee at City Hall (2 yrs) – reviewing the efficacy of recovery programs and setting guidelines for future recovery programs within the city of Abbotsford

Abbotsford Christian Leaders Network (10 yrs) – serving the community through initiatives like large faith-based events that unified the city, Love Abbotsford which mobilized the community with intentional acts of kindness; and empowered people to bring to fruition ministry ideas & passions like the Cyrus Centre and Psalm 23 Transition Society. 

Conservative Policy Priorities

Korky is setting out to make positive change in the current provincial political climate

Policy Priorities:

Education

Remove Ideology from the classroom – Schools must be places of learning – not tools for activism or indoctrination.

Support parent choices – Parents have the right to determine how and where their children will be educated.

Healthcare

Serious Substantive Reform – Chronic shortages in physicians, nurses and ICU capacity has become painstakingly clear. It’s time for serious reform

More doctors, more nurses – prioritizing government funding and support for post-secondary programs and students

Economy

Lower taxes, smaller government – Wasteful spending should be cut and the savings returned to taxpayers

Champion small and medium-sized business – Useless and redundant regulations need to be removed

Korky is passionate, energetic and committed. He represent the Abbotsford West Riding whole-heartedly as the MLA. His interest in people, awareness of the connection between community and provincial issues, and his strong family values will benefit this region.

Name: Lakhwinder Jhaj
Bio:
Lakhwinder has deep roots in the Fraser Valley. She immigrated to Canada from India with her family as a child in 1976 and settled in Mission, where she attended school. After later moving to Aldergrove and then Penticton, she returned to the Fraser Valley in 2010 and has called the region home ever since. Her family’s farm on Huntington Road, along with more than 20 years of experience operating a construction company and used vehicle dealership, have kept her closely connected to the people, businesses and agricultural community of Abbotsford–Mission.

Lakhwinder’s community service has been recognized through a citizenship award from Citizenship and Immigration Canada, the B.C. Community Achievement Award, and a Chamber of Commerce Woman of the Year Award. She has also been recognized in regional publications for her community leadership and public service.

Lakhwinder brings considerable political and electoral experience. She ran for the BC NDP in Boundary-Similkameen in the 2009 provincial election, receiving 5,870 votes and approximately 32.9 per cent of the vote. She later ran for the BC NDP in Abbotsford South in 2013, receiving 4,210 votes. In 2021, Lakhwinder represented the Liberal Party of Canada in Skeena–Bulkley Valley, receiving 2,866 votes in the federal election.

Lakhwinder’s political experience reflects a willingness to work across traditional party lines. Although she has represented different parties over the years, her focus has remained on community service, practical solutions and bringing people together. That experience is consistent with CentreBC’s approach as a broad, centrist party open to British Columbians from different political backgrounds.

As CentreBC’s candidate for Abbotsford–Mission, Lakhwinder brings community leadership, business experience and an understanding of the issues affecting families, farmers, seniors, newcomers and small-business owners. She believes politics should be practical, respectful and focused on the priorities of the people who live and work in the community. Lakhwinder is committed to listening, finding common ground and representing Abbotsford–Mission with a clear focus on local priorities.

Name: Darryl Kropp
Bio:
Daryl Kropp is the Conservative Party of BC candidate in Abbotsford-Mission. 

Darryl has called Abbotsford home for more than 25 years. He and Corina, his wife of 30 years, raised their three children here. He has served on the board of Northview Community Church for 17 years, including 11 years as Chair.

Over more than two decades, Darryl has led major technology and organizational transformation initiatives in utilities, aerospace, and human services. At Cascade Aerospace in Abbotsford, he built the lean management system that transformed company operations. Today, he leads large-scale human services implementations at RedMane Technology and has helped build child welfare systems for Indigenous communities across Canada. 

Darryl brings extensive governance and financial oversight experience. In 2018, members elected him to the board of First West Credit Union (Envision Financial), where he helped oversee one of British Columbia’s largest financial cooperatives, with more than $20 billion in assets. During his tenure, he chaired the Governance and Nominations Committee, served as Vice-Chair of the Risk, Investment and Loan Committee, and helped guide First West through its transition to Tru Cooperative Bank.

He holds the ICD.D designation from the Rotman School of Management, where he was class valedictorian, and is a certified Lean Black Belt and Project Management Professional (PMP). His track record is built on fiscal responsibility, effective governance, and getting meaningful results for the people he serves.

Name: Pam Alexis
Bio:
An experienced voice for Abbotsford-Mission.

Pam Alexis has lived all over the world, but she knew she was finally home when she and her family moved to the Fraser Valley. An active community member focused on helping people, Pam has served on the boards of the Mission Chamber of Commerce and the Mission Rotary Club. She was elected Mayor of Mission in 2018 and served as the MLA for Abbotsford-Mission from 2020 to 2024. As an MLA, Pam also served in cabinet as BC's Minister of Agriculture and Food, helping champion BC's food growers and producers in the Fraser Valley and beyond.

On housing and healthcare and affordability and everything in between, you can count on Pam Alexis and David Eby and the BC NDP team to fight for you.

Name: Donegal Wilson
Bio:
Donegal Wilson is a dedicated leader and community advocate, and the Conservative Party of BC MLA for Boundary-Similkameen. With a deep commitment to her community and extensive experience in business management and non-profit leadership, Donegal aims to bring effective representation to the region.

Personal Life

Born in Summerland, BC, and raised on a cattle ranch in the Otter Valley near Tulameen, Donegal developed a deep connection to the land, a strong work ethic, and a love for animals and community. She graduated from Princeton Secondary and moved to Northwest BC for community college, beginning her career in administration. Donegal lives in Keremeos with her husband where they own and operate Direct Performance, a small engine business. Known for her quick thinking, decision-making skills, and financial acumen, Donegal is committed to her community both personally and professionally.

Professional Background

Donegal’s career began in administration with various small businesses and non-profit organizations. Her experience includes working for Central Mountain Air and founding Direct Performance with her husband. In 2012, she became the Executive Director of the BC Snowmobile Federation, where she has led efforts to strengthen organized snowmobiling, worked with all levels of government, and collaborated with industry and community organizations. Her role requires a diverse skill set, including legislative development, stakeholder engagement, and financial management.

Community Involvement

Donegal’s commitment to community service is evident through her extensive volunteer work and leadership roles. She is a long-time advocate for outdoor recreation, serving as a key figure in the BC Snowmobile Federation. Her work involves collaborating with local and provincial government officials, marketing associations, and other outdoor recreation groups. Known for her ability to get things done, Donegal has a track record of making informed decisions and leading by example.

Vision

Donegal envisions a thriving Boundary-Similkameen that retains its roots while forging a strong path forward. Her vision includes supporting economic development, enhancing healthcare services, and bolstering support for small businesses. Donegal aims to implement practical solutions to address the unique challenges of the region, such as promoting sustainable tourism, improving infrastructure, and fostering community well-being. She is committed to representing all residents with respect and integrity, ensuring that the Similkameen Boundary prospers and remains a vibrant region for future generations.

Name: Roly Russell
Bio:
Standing up for Boundary-Similkameen.

Born and raised in rural Grand Forks, Roly Russell is a father of two who is passionate about lowering costs for families, strengthening agriculture and food security, and building an economy that works for everyone in rural BC.

As a local leader, he worked tirelessly to help people in need and coordinate disaster recovery during the devastating floods in Grand Forks in 2018. He stepped up again to help communities with disaster recovery following the atmospheric rivers in 2021. He has served as a tireless advocate for rural communities across BC, working across ministries to help deliver solutions that work for rural people.

Roly knows that people in our communities have been through a lot — from the pandemic, to global inflation and climate-related disasters. He knows that’s why it’s more important than ever that we have a leader who’s on our side, rather than paving the way for powerful interests that take advantage of people again.

Roly Russell, David Eby and the BC NDP are looking out for everyday families. You can count on them to fight for you on what matters to people here.

Name: Sharon Hartwell
Bio:
A Dedicated Advocate for Bulkley Valley-Stikine

Sharon is deeply rooted in the Bulkley Valley, a place she proudly calls home. Born and raised in this picturesque rural area, she has not only built her life here but has also instilled her values of community engagement and growth in her two sons, who have chosen to remain in the same region.

Community-Minded from the Start

From an early age, Sharon was raised to be community-minded and to actively participate in shaping the future of her beloved community and its surroundings. Her commitment was to elevate the standards for small communities within the riding and beyond.

A Vision for Community Development

As a business owner, Sharon recognized the need to showcase the beauty and potential of her community to the outside world. She sought to promote the area’s natural beauty and economic opportunities while encouraging business growth.

From Village Council to Mayoral Leadership

Sharon’s dedication to her community led her to run for the Village Council in Telkwa, where she served a term and a half. Her desire to make a more significant impact drove her to run for the position of Mayor, where she spent an impressive 12 years championing the interests of small and rural communities. During her tenure, she engaged with Provincial and Federal Governments to address crucial issues facing these communities.

Team BC: Celebrating Community Beauty

Sharon’s innovative program, Team BC, celebrated the splendor of small and rural communities in British Columbia. It became a resounding success with all 82 communities participating, highlighting their unique attributes.

Infrastructure and Partnership Advocacy

Recognizing the need for infrastructure development, Sharon represented small communities as the Small Community Representative at UBCM. She successfully lobbied for a grant process that transformed the relationship between these communities and the Provincial and Federal Governments, promoting a partnership approach rather than dependency.

Championing Health and Transportation

Sharon has always been a champion of healthcare and infrastructure. Her leadership as the chair of the North West Regional Hospital District saw improvements in healthcare delivery, including the construction of a new hospital in Masset. To address the need for more healthcare professionals, she initiated the Northern Health Connections Bus, a program that provides vital transportation for medical appointments and post-hospital discharge.

A Strong Advocate on the National Stage

Recognizing the importance of representation at the national level, Sharon ran and was elected to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM). Here, she actively participated in the Rural Forum and successfully advocated for changes in the infrastructure formula for rural communities in Canada.

Safety and Infrastructure Advocacy

Sharon’s commitment to safety led her to become Vice-Chair of Transportation and Infrastructure for FCM, where she oversaw airport-related matters. She also joined the Safety Committee, representing all Canadian communities in rail safety issues.

Environmental and Technological Innovation

In her role as a director on the FCM Board, Sharon served on the Environment Committee, exploring innovative technological solutions to enhance communities.

A 20-Year Journey of Service

Throughout her 20-year journey in public service, Sharon has consistently worked towards building strong and healthy communities. Her unwavering commitment is to be a resounding voice for the people of the Bulkley Valley-Stikine Riding, advocating for positive change and a brighter future for all.

Name: Vikas Gautam
Bio:
Through his experience in communications, community engagement, and multicultural event organization, Vikas has connected with people from diverse backgrounds and communities. His experience has taught him the importance of listening, building relationships, bringing people together, and turning community ideas into action.

Vikas is running as the CentreBC candidate for Burnaby Centre, bringing his community experience and commitment to public service to provincial politics.

Sign up to stay informed and receive news from CentreBC:

Name: Joshua Domnich
Bio:
Joshua Domnich is the Conservative Party of BC Candidate for Burnaby Centre.

Joshua cares deeply and is very passionate about our world. Joshua has a best effort philosophy in all aspects of his life and he believes “bad things happen when good people do nothing”. He also believes that serving others starts with listening and showing up. Joshua is running for MLA because he believes in accountability and integrity in government and he knows he can make a substantial positive impact for the constituents of Burnaby Centre.

Joshua holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in Criminology from the Burnaby campus of Simon Fraser University. He also graduated from a secondary school English and French Immersion program, is bilingual, and was the valedictorian of his graduating class.

Joshua’s career has given him experience in public service at both the federal and provincial levels. He served as a Community Liaison Officer for a federal Conservative MP, working directly with constituents, coordinating meetings, conducting research, supporting communications, and building relationships with community organizations and government stakeholders. At the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia, he served as a Legislative

Assistant for the Conservative Party of BC caucus, supporting four MLAs with legislative work, scheduling, stakeholder relations and research. Joshua has also worked extensively in campaign organization. He has significant experience as a Campaign Manager and Deputy Campaign Manager, as well as a Treasurer on a provincial conservative Riding Association.

Before entering public service, Joshua spent more than a decade in landscaping operations and management, supervising teams, managing projects, working with clients, and keeping complex operations on track.

Joshua is bringing that experience to Burnaby Centre, with a commitment to listening to residents, working hard, and representing the community with accountability, integrity and dedication.

Name: Shila Taheri
Bio:
Shila Taheri is a labour leader, legal researcher, published author, and human rights advocate running to represent Burnaby Centre. Her work has been guided by a commitment to fairness, accountability, and ensuring that people have a meaningful voice in the decisions that affect their lives.

She believes effective representation requires careful attention to evidence, a willingness to ask difficult questions, and the courage to challenge decisions when people are not being heard. Her experience in labour relations, legal research, public service, and organizational governance has given her a detailed understanding of how laws and policies can shape people’s everyday lives.

Her education and professional experience in law have shaped her approach to advocacy and public service. Shila holds an LL.M. in International Business Law and an LL.B., and has pursued further Canadian studies in immigration and labour law. She is a published legal researcher and author whose work includes scholarly books and articles in areas such as international business law and arbitration.

Through her union work, Shila has represented workers in grievances, workplace disputes, and investigations, advocated for safer and more respectful workplaces, and helped people understand and exercise their rights. She also serves in several elected leadership roles within the BC General Employees’ Union (BCGEU), including First Vice-Chair of Local 803, Chair of the Component 8 Membership Committee, and Recording Secretary of Component 8.

As a wife and mother of two boys, Shila also brings a personal perspective to the challenges facing families and communities. Her priorities include affordability and housing, strong and reliable public services, good jobs and respect for working people, safe communities, and protecting the environment for future generations.

Shila is running to represent the people of Burnaby Centre with the same approach she has brought to her advocacy: listening closely, doing the work, asking tough questions, and making sure the everyday realities of the community are heard in the Legislature.

Name: Anne Kang
Bio:
Anne Kang: Protecting and supporting people in Burnaby Centre

Anne Kang has called Burnaby home for more than 40 years, and serving her community has always been at the heart of what she does.

A former Burnaby teacher and three-term Burnaby City Councillor, Anne has spent her career empowering citizens, listening and collaborating with people, bringing their concerns forward, and making government more accessible and responsive.

As MLA for Burnaby Centre since 2017, Anne has worked to protect the services that people rely on, whether that’s strengthening public health care and education, expanding opportunity, or supporting seniors and families. She understands that behind every policy is real people who want to be heard, treated fairly, and given a chance to thrive.

Anne is passionate about standing up for British Columbians, especially those facing barriers to accessing services and opportunities.

Where the conservative parties would cozy up to Trump, Anne Kang, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for our province and our country, protect and support people who need it, and build a strong, independent economy.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.

Name: Peter Si
Bio:
Peter Si is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Burnaby East.

Peter moved to Burnaby at age 12 and has called the community home ever since. He is a graduate of the University of Alberta, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science, History and International Studies.

Peter began his career on a municipal election campaign in Vancouver. That experience taught him what politics is really about: representing people and giving those who need help a voice at the highest levels of government.

Since then, he has worked on campaigns at the municipal, provincial and federal levels. He served as provincial campaign manager for Steve Kooner in Richmond-Queensborough in 2024, and as federal campaign director for James Yan in Burnaby Centre in 2025. He has also served as President of the Richmond-Queensborough riding association since 2024, and as Vice-President of the Burnaby Centre Electoral District Association.

For the past two years, Peter has worked in Victoria for the Conservative caucus, supporting elected members as they hold the government to account.

Name: Javad Shushtarian
Bio:
Javad recently completed a Bachelor of Science in Nursing at BCIT and is in the process of obtaining his nursing licence in British Columbia. During his nursing education, he completed placements in hospitals, urgent care centres and supervised injection sites across the Lower Mainland, gaining firsthand experience with challenges including primary care shortages and long emergency-room wait times.

Javad also holds a Bachelor of Science in Biology from Simon Fraser University, where he developed a strong interest in environmental conservation and the relationship between the environment and community health. He believes health is shaped not only by access to medical care, but also by housing, financial stability, social supports, transportation and the physical environment.

His healthcare and community work has also included co-presenting a workshop on decolonizing and Indigenizing health-science education and organizing a health-promotion initiative at the Tsleil-Waututh Nation Health Fair focused on cervical cancer screening and HPV vaccination.

Javad is running in Burnaby East to advocate for accessible healthcare, affordable housing, reliable transit and stronger community supports, with a focus on the social and environmental conditions that shape people’s health and quality of life.

Name: Rohini Arora
Bio:
Building a stronger economy for people and families in Burnaby East

Rohini Arora is the candidate for Burnaby East. She was first elected in 2024 and served as Deputy Chair of the BC Government Caucus. Prior to public life, Rohini served as the Director of Organizing and Campaigns at the BC Federation of Labour. She has over a decade of experience lifting up youth across the country, and mentoring them in civic engagement.

Growing up in Burnaby East’s Westridge neighbourhood, Rohini saw firsthand what happens when governments refuse to protect people by making deep cuts to important programs and services. She then devoted her energies to standing up for people and workers and making their lives better.

Rohini Arora, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for our province, to protect people and services, and to build a stronger economy.

Name: Simon Chandler
Bio:
Simon Chandler has called North Burnaby home for the past fifteen years. He grew up in Burnaby Heights and now lives in the Brentwood area, giving him a firsthand understanding of what matters most to the people of Burnaby North.

Simon is a strong supporter of those who serve and protect our communities. As a Community Police Volunteer for three years, he gained direct experience in crime prevention and saw the challenges officers face in responding to the drug crisis. That experience reinforced his belief that police need the right tools to tackle crime and keep neighbourhoods safe. His commitment to service began as an army cadet and continued in the Canadian Army Reserves, where he served as an infantry soldier.

Simon graduated from Trinity Western University with a Bachelor of Business Administration in accounting. Working in public practice accounting, he advised clients on federal and provincial tax matters, helped businesses operate more efficiently and supported those hit by pandemic restrictions. He will bring that expertise to Victoria as an advocate for common-sense tax policy.

After graduating, Simon attended the Laurentian Leadership Centre in Ottawa, studying good governance and the legacies of Canada’s prime ministers while interning as a policy analyst in the food and beverage industry. He was recognized for his leadership and earned a Certificate in Leadership and Applied Public Affairs.

Outside of work, Simon enjoys hiking, whitewater rafting and camping along the Squamish River. He is an avid reader of history and a guitar player.

Name: Janet Routledge
Bio: MLA for Burnaby North

Name: David Xie
Bio:
David Xie is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Burnaby South-Metrotown.

David Xie has called Burnaby home for nearly a decade, where he lives with his wife and their son. Raised by immigrant parents, David grew up in Metro Vancouver and graduated from the University of British Columbia.

For more than a decade, David has built his career in recruitment and talent acquisition, working with businesses and professionals in Canada and internationally. His work has given him firsthand experience with the challenges employers face in finding skilled people, building strong teams and growing their businesses.

David’s involvement in the community began with working alongside residents on issues affecting their neighbourhoods and families. He has worked with residents on local issues, helping ensure community concerns are heard and understood by decision-makers.

As MLA for Burnaby South-Metrotown, David would bring that community experience to Victoria and work to ensure the concerns of local residents are heard in the decisions that affect their families and neighbourhoods.

Name: Paul Choi
Bio:
Paul Choi: Standing up for people in Burnaby South-Metrotown

Paul Choi is standing up to Donald Trump’s unfair tariffs and fighting to protect B.C. jobs, businesses and economic future.

First elected as MLA for Burnaby South–Metrotown in 2024, he served as Parliamentary Secretary for Trade in the Ministry of Jobs and Economic Growth and as First Vice-President of the Pacific NorthWest Economic Region (PNWER), working to strengthen trade relationships, open new markets and reduce reliance on the United States.

A former police officer with experience as a small business owner and lawyer, Paul is also a Qualified Mediator and Arbitrator. He is seeking re-election to protect livelihoods, support local businesses and build a stronger, more secure future for Burnaby South–Metrotown.

Paul Choi, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect the services that matter to families and build a stronger economy.

The plan is working. We can’t stop now.

Name: Andrew Rose
Bio:
Born and raised in Ontario’s Niagara region, Andrew studied computer science at Brock University, concentrating on artificial intelligence and software systems design. After his studies he moved to Seattle to work at Amazon.com, remaining there until 2002, when he relocated to British Columbia. He now lives in Burnaby South with his wife, son, and daughter.

Across the province, he has helped organizations improve the way they deliver value and services.

He also volunteers close to home, serving on the parent advisory council at the school his children attend, helping to run his strata, and pulling together events that bring the neighbourhood together. He believes that if we do not put in the work to preserve the things we find beautiful, they have a habit of going away, and he is always on the lookout for that.

He is equally committed to small and medium-sized businesses, and to making sure they have a place to grow and compete in our regional communities, with less red tape standing in the way.

Andrew is looking to put his skills in business architecture, organization, and systems design to use with OneBC.

Name: Joe Latam
Bio:
Joe Latam is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Burnaby-New Westminster.

Born and raised in British Columbia, Joe is a member of Métis Nation BC.

He is a graduate of the University of British Columbia, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science. While at UBC, Joe served as Treasurer of the UBC Young Conservatives and advocated for free expression and common-sense policies on campus.

Joe brings experience from both the public and private sectors. He began his career working in British Columbia’s agriculture and manufacturing industries, giving him first-hand experience with two sectors that play an important role in the province’s economy and communities.

For the past two years, Joe has worked for the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia,

helping British Columbians navigate government processes and access the programs and

services they need. His experience working with people dealing directly with government has

strengthened his commitment to practical, accountable public service.

Joe is seeking office to bring his experience in British Columbia’s private sector and provincial

government to the Legislature, with a focus on practical solutions and ensuring government

works effectively for the people it serves.

Name: Raj Chouhan
Bio:
Standing up for you and your family in Burnaby-New Westminster.

Raj Chouhan moved to Canada in 1973, and has spent his career fighting for regular people. Elected six times as an MLA, Raj is the first South Asian person to serve as Speaker of the House in the BC legislature. He is the founding President of the Canadian Farmworkers’ Union and the founding member of the BC Organization to Fight Racism, and he knows that regular people need a government that works for them, not the rich and the powerful.

Raj believes that people in Burnaby-New Westminster need a government that is ready to stand up for them and protect what matters - supporting workers and businesses facing tariffs, bringing down the costs people face, or strengthening the healthcare that British Columbians rely on.

The conservative parties would cozy up to Trump and cut services.

Raj Chouhan, David Eby and the BC NDP team have a plan to stand up to Trump, lower costs, hire more healthcare workers, and build a strong and independent economy.

Name: Lorne Doerkson
Bio:
Lorne Doerkson isn’t a guy working the room with talking points. He’s the one you’d find at the rodeo instead, doing the work quietly, locally, and without forgetting who he serves.

Lorne is a long-time Cariboo resident who has spent close to thirty years in the communities he represents. Born in New Westminster and raised in Surrey, he built a life in Williams Lake. He spent twenty years as a Black Press newspaper publisher before moving into financial planning, and was a small-business owner, Rotary president, rodeo announcer, and avid volunteer, voted Stampede volunteer of the year in 2019. He is a husband and father of two daughters.

In August 2026, when the South Cariboo faced a state of emergency, Lorne stepped up for the community while staying present and calm. He stayed close to the people living under threat, pushed the government for help when communities were at risk, and showed leadership during his neighbours’ most difficult moments.

Lorne’s background is the work of someone who knows, community by community, how a mill town, a ranch, a main street, and an organization actually hold together. He knows how to show leadership through a crisis and stand up for his home.

In September, when his colleagues asked him to lead British Columbians through the 45th General Election, he accepted, and within 48 hours, brought the party back together as one team.

Lorne is running to be Premier of the most beautiful place in the world. The caucus is with him, and British Columbians are ready for a Premier who puts them first: safer streets, an affordable life, and certainty that what they’ve built is theirs to keep. David Eby called this election to save himself. Lorne is running to be Premier to stand up for BC, for change.

Name: Kathryn Askew
Bio:
Building BC strong in Cariboo-Chilcotin

Kathryn Askew is a retired public school teacher with 32 years of experience in education and a long record of union and community service. She served in leadership roles with the BCTF and her local teachers’ union, including as local president and bargaining chair, and received a national award for innovative teaching.

Kathryn Askew, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to create jobs, protect healthcare, and make life more affordable.

Name: Dan Grice
Bio:
Dan Grice is a leading real estate and estate planning lawyer in the Fraser Valley and a passionate advocate for his clients. With 12 years of legal experience, he has assisted thousands of clients in purchasing homes, establishing businesses and organizing their affairs. He is a member of the Fraser Valley technical tax group and other associations and has received scholastic awards in tax law.

Having grown up in the Fraser Valley, Dan has resided in North Chilliwack since graduating from Robson Hall Law School in 2013 and is deeply invested in the community. As a parent of two children in Chilliwack schools, he is acutely aware of the challenges students and educators face in an ever-evolving world.

After having previously run as an independent candidate, Dan joined the CentreBC team for the opportunity to work alongside Andrew Weaver and Elenore Sturko, a team that prioritizes intelligent policies and people. He aims to provide a voice for those in Chilliwack and the millions of British Columbians who desire government to focus on the economy and are increasingly frustrated by left-wing and right-wing populists.

Dan’s passion for public service and government extends far back. Having studied classical history and archaeology at the University of British Columbia, he served in the student alma mater society and enjoyed studying the development of democratic systems throughout history. Over the last two decades, Dan has served as an organizer on the 2005 and 2009 referendums on electoral reform, as well as a proponent in the 2018 referendum. As a law student, he co-authored a paper for Elections Canada on voting modernization.

A strong advocate for professional independence, Dan is ready to take his legal skills to Victoria and to help push back against government overreach while protecting the most vulnerable.

Name: Heather Maahs
Bio:
Experience:

Heather’s journey in advocacy began in 2008 when she successfully ran for a seat as a school trustee in Chilliwack. Her consistent electoral victories over the last fifteen years, in five subsequent elections, underscore the trust and confidence her community places in her leadership. Throughout her tenure, Heather has consistently championed foundational reading skill attainment, emphasizing the critical role of literacy in the learning process. Her belief that “First, we learn to read, then we read to learn” has become a guiding principle in her approach to education.

Championing Education:

Heather’s advocacy extends beyond her role as a school trustee. She recognizes the need for systemic and purposeful changes in the provincial education system, advocating for legislative measures to address these challenges. A strong proponent of parental rights, Heather believes in respecting and supporting parents’ goals to raise healthy and responsible young individuals. Her vision emphasizes that children do not belong solely to schools or governments; rather, parental rights should be supported by legislation to ensure a collaborative and supportive educational environment.

In her pursuit of a provincial role as a Member of the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia, Heather brings a wealth of experience, a deep sense of community involvement, and a steadfast commitment to championing education. Her advocacy extends beyond political aspirations, rooted in a genuine desire to contribute positively to the well-being of her community and the education system as a whole.

Community Involvement:

Heather’s commitment to her community is evident through her active involvement in various initiatives and organizations. She took specialized training in Orton Gillingham tutoring and Early Assessment from the University of Hull, Great Britain, showcasing her dedication to enhancing educational methods. For many years, she moderated an email listserv where stakeholders, including school trustees, parents, teachers, and ministry officials, engaged in discussions on education issues. This platform facilitated the exchange of data, research, and articles, fostering a collaborative approach to addressing educational challenges.

Family First:

In 1993, Heather and her husband made the significant decision to move their young family from North Vancouver to Chilliwack, BC. Together, they ran a construction company, navigating the challenges and rewards of entrepreneurship. Tragically, Heather’s husband unexpectedly passed away in 2009, marking a profound moment of change in their lives.

Heather is exceedingly proud of her three adult children, highlighting the joy and fulfillment they bring to her life. Additionally, she embraces the role of “Nan” with enthusiasm, cherishing her relationships with eleven incredible grandchildren. For Heather, family is not only a source of personal fulfillment but also a driving force behind her commitment to making the world a better place for future generations.

Her experiences as a mother and grandmother have undoubtedly shaped her perspective on community service and advocacy, emphasizing the importance of creating a positive and nurturing environment for all families.

As Heather ventures into he role as MLA for Chilliwack North, her dedication to family values remains evident, guiding her aspirations to contribute to a better future for her loved ones and the broader community.

Name: Á’a:líya Warbus
Bio:
Personal Background

Á’a:líya (A’aliya) Warbus was born and raised in Stó:lō Territory, and has deep family roots in politics and activism, as the daughter of Former Lieutenant Governor of British Columbia Steven Lewis Point, OC OBC (Xwĕ lī qwĕl tĕl). Point (Xwĕ lī qwĕl tĕl) served as tribal chair of the Stó:lō Nation and Grand Chief of Stó:lō Tribal Council, the chiefs’ representative for the Stó:lō Nation Government House, and Chief Commissioner of the British Columbia Treaty Commission.

As a mother of three children aged 13, 11, and 3, Á’a:líya is personally invested in building a better future for her family and community. Her upbringing and family life have played a crucial role in shaping her commitment to Indigenous rights, cultural preservation, and community well-being.

Educational Attainment

Á’a:líya is an alumna of the University of British Columbia, where she earned a Master of Fine Arts in Film Production. This academic journey allowed her to delve into the complexities of Indigenous identity and worldview within the context of contemporary society. This educational background has been crucial in shaping her perspectives and contributing to her expertise in the field.

Professional Experience

Director of Cultural Communications at Stó:lō Xwexwilmexw Government: Currently serving as the Director of Cultural Communications, Á’a:líya plays a pivotal role in facilitating communication and understanding between the Stó:lō Xwexwilmexw Government and the broader community. This position underscores her commitment to preserving and promoting Indigenous culture while engaging with various stakeholders.

Professor at Capilano University – Indigenous Digital Film Department: In her role as a Professor in the Indigenous Digital Film department at Capilano University, Á’a:líya contributes to the education and empowerment of the next generation of Indigenous filmmakers. Her teaching role reflects her dedication to passing on knowledge and fostering creativity within the Indigenous community.

Multifaceted Artist: As a filmmaker, podcast host, actor, and musician, Á’a:líya has built an extensive collection of multi-disciplinary art over the course of her career. Her work has been showcased at numerous film and music festivals, community events, and exhibits since 2005. This artistic dimension not only showcases her creativity but also serves as a powerful medium for expressing the struggles and triumphs of her people.

Advocacy and Community Engagement: Á’a:líya has been actively involved in advocacy work, especially in uplifting the voices of Indigenous youth. Working on the front lines, she directly engages with young individuals, amplifying their perspectives and providing support for their growth. Her commitment extends to contributing to program and media deliverables that promote success within Indigenous communities.

Podcasting and Online Engagement: Á’a:líya started podcasting as part of her role with Stó:lō Xwexwilmexw Government, using this platform to reflect the everyday work of her people toward sustainability and growth. The podcast also serves as an educational resource, shedding light on the history of Stó:lō language, governance, and the deep connection to the land.

Name: Kelli Paddon
Bio:
Kelli Paddon: Building up Chilliwack-Cultus Lake

Kelli Paddon is a community leader and a mother of two with strong roots in Chilliwack, committed to helping families build a good life for themselves. A former Member of the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia and Parliamentary Secretary for Gender Equity, Kelli brings extensive experience in public service, leadership, and community engagement.

She is the Founder of Equiiti Strategic, a Chilliwack-based small business where she provides strategic guidance, leadership coaching, and practical support to organizations and leaders navigating growth, change, and complex challenges.

She knows that families in Chillwack-Cultus Lake need a government that is willing to stand up for them, help make things easier, and protect the things that people depend on.

The conservative parties would cozy up to Trump and cut healthcare and education.

Kelli Paddon, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to keep fighting back - to lower costs, recruit more healthcare workers, and build an economy free from the United States.

Name: Scott McInnis
Bio:
Scott McInnis is a dedicated educator and community leader who has proudly called Kimberley, British Columbia, home since 2010. Originally from a small farming community in Ontario, Scott has built a life in the East Kootenays with his wife, Diana, and their teenage son, Luke.

Career
For the past 15 years, Scott has worked as a teacher and principal, serving students from Pre-K to Grade 12 in both public and independent school systems. His career has made him a passionate advocate for education and child care, actively engaging in these issues at both the local and provincial levels. Scott’s commitment to education extends beyond the classroom, as he has successfully coached basketball teams to multiple East Kootenay Zone Championships.

Community Involvement
Scott McInnis is deeply involved in his community. He and his family are avid outdoor enthusiasts, participating in activities like hunting, fly fishing, and managing their family Christmas tree hobby business. Scott’s dedication to community leadership is evident through his active participation in the Elks Lodge #90 in Kimberley, where he volunteers for various events throughout the year. His passion for parliamentary democracy was further ignited in 2022 when he was selected to participate in the Teacher Institute for Parliamentary Democracy in Victoria, marking the beginning of his journey into politics.

Name: Andrea Dunlop
Bio:
Andrea Dunlop: taking action for people in Columbia River-Revelstoke.

Andrea Dunlop was a high school teacher for three decades, and has deep roots in her community. She grew up in small town BC, built her career there, and helped successive generations of small town British Columbians enter the world as active and engaged citizens.

A ten-year board member of the Windermere Community Association, she wants to tackle the big challenges we all face with rigorous and evidence-based action. That’s why she’s running with David Eby and the BC NDP: to build homes for people, to strengthen our healthcare system, and to grow a strong and clean economy.

Andrea Dunlop, David Eby and the BC NDP are ready to take on the big challenges facing you and your family.

Name: Ryan Peterson
Bio:
Ryan Peterson is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Coquitlam–Burke Mountain.

Ryan is a job creator who has spent his career building businesses in British Columbia. In 2011, he co-founded Finger Food Studios in Port Coquitlam and grew it into a technology company with 200 good local jobs, helping some of the world’s largest companies, from LEGO and Microsoft to PACCAR, solve their toughest problems. Finger Food was named B.C. Exporter of the Year in 2017.

Ryan and his wife of 17 years, Monica, have lived in the Tri-Cities since 2014, where they are raising their three boys in local public schools. Monica runs Apex Fencing in Port Moody. Ryan believes he lives in the greatest place on earth, and he’s making sure his boys know it too. From early-morning hockey practices to fishing trips up the coast and ski days in the mountains, he’s taking them to every edge of British Columbia.

After Finger Food was acquired by Unity Technologies, Ryan led a global division of more than 1,000 people, including its advanced technology and AI teams. He now backs early-stage technology companies, several of them in B.C., and the jobs they create. In 2026, B.C.’s business leaders elected him Chair of the Business Council of British Columbia; he has stepped away from that role to seek election. Ryan was named Tri-Cities Business Leader of the Year in 2019, received the King Charles III Coronation Medal in 2025, and serves on the board of the Rick Hansen Foundation.

Name: Jodie Wickens
Bio:
Jodie Wickens: Standing up for people in Coquitlam-Burke Mountain

Elected to the BC legislature in 2016 as the youngest woman MLA, and elected again in 2024, Jodie Wickens has a long history of public service. In government she served as the Minister of Children and Family Development. Prior to her election in 2024, she was an advocate for public education and social justice, holding an executive leadership position as Director of Programs and Services for Child and Youth Programs at a large non-profit.

In office, she’s fought for people every day, and been part of a team that has connected a million more people to a family doctor, brought down housing costs, and created new jobs.

Jodie Wickens, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect the services that people count on, and build our economy for the future. The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.

Name: Matt Cole
Bio:
Matthew Cole was born and raised in British Columbia and has lived here his whole life, mostly in the Lower Mainland, with time in Kelowna and Victoria as well.

Matthew holds a master’s degree in exercise physiology from the University of Victoria and a Bachelor of Kinesiology from the University of British Columbia.

For the last 26 years, he has worked as a kinesiologist and has owned his own business for the last 23 years, focused on the field of occupational rehabilitation.

In recent years, he has been disheartened by the direction British Columbia has been going and has joined the OneBC team to help turn things around.

Name: Matt Liang
Bio:
Matt Liang is Conservative Party of BC candidate for Coquitlam-Maillardville.

Matt is a longtime public servant who has dedicated his career to helping people, supporting community safety and making a positive difference in the lives of others. He has served as a Deputy Sheriff, worked with young people as a Child Care Counsellor, and helped keep workplaces safe as a health and safety facilitator for the BC Public Service and the BC General Employees’ Union. That work has shown him the challenges facing British Columbia firsthand, and it has inspired him to fight for change

Matt believes strong communities are built through service, personal responsibility, compassion and people working together to find practical solutions. Whether protecting the public, supporting youth or helping his neighbours, his focus has always been the same: helping people and making a difference. Matt Liang is ready to get to work on day one.

Name: Jennifer Blatherwick
Bio: MLA for Coquitlam-Maillardville

Name: Jason Cook
Bio: Jason’s decision to become more involved in public life is also deeply personal. The loss of his mother in 2024, following his family’s difficult experience with British Columbia’s healthcare system, prompted him to take a closer look at where the system is falling short and how it can be improved. Over the past two years, he has researched ways to improve the efficiency and delivery of healthcare and has identified practical changes designed to deliver tangible benefits for patients and the public. That work reinforced his belief that better outcomes are possible when government is willing to listen, learn, and act—and that difficult experiences can be turned into constructive action that benefits others. That search led Jason to become involved with the emerging CentreBC movement in February 2025 and its commitment to evidence-based policy, fiscal responsibility, collaboration, and practical solutions. He is seeking public office not simply to identify what is wrong, but to help deliver meaningful results—from healthcare and affordability to housing, public safety, economic opportunity, and a government that works effectively for his community and all British Columbians.

Name: Brennan Day
Bio:
Brennan Day is a dedicated leader with a deep commitment to the Comox Valley, who served as the Executive Director of the Eureka Support Society. His extensive experience in business management and community service positions him as a key advocate for transformative change in the region.

A Longtime Resident and Advocate

A long-time resident of the Comox Valley, Brennan Day’s roots run deep in the community he passionately serves. His journey into leadership has been driven by a genuine desire to make a meaningful impact. Brennan’s background includes managing large-scale international projects and founding a successful industrial supply, manpower, and training firm. These experiences have provided him with unique insights into the diverse needs of the Comox Valley.

Champion of Mental Health and Community Well-Being

Brennan is a staunch advocate for addressing critical issues facing the Comox Valley. As Executive Director of the Eureka Support Society, he has led initiatives to enhance mental health support and community well-being. His dedication to these causes underscores his commitment to improving the quality of life for all residents.

A Multifaceted Career Path

Before focusing on community service, Brennan built a distinguished career in international project management and business. His work overseeing complex projects and driving organizational success has equipped him with the skills and knowledge necessary to tackle local challenges effectively.

Experience, Passion, and Vision

Brennan’s leadership is defined by a blend of experience, passion, and vision. His comprehensive background in both global and local contexts enables him to bridge gaps and drive positive change. Brennan is committed to implementing practical solutions to address homelessness, substance abuse, and mental health issues, aiming to restore stability and safety to the Courtenay-Comox community. With his proven ability to lead and transform organizations, Brennan is well-prepared to guide the Comox Valley toward a brighter and more prosperous future.

Name: Jay Van Oostdam
Bio:
Jay Van Oostdam is a veterinarian, public health professional and longtime environmental advocate with decades of experience working on the connections between human health and the environment.

Jay was born in Yellowknife and grew up in Regina. He earned a Bachelor of Science in Biology from the University of Regina and later completed a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine at the University of Saskatchewan. He began practising veterinary medicine in Nanaimo and later worked across British Columbia and Saskatchewan.

He went on to complete post-doctoral work at the University of British Columbia’s Pulmonary Research Laboratory and a Master of Public Health in Environmental Health and Epidemiology at the University of Minnesota. That work led to a 25-year career with Health Canada and BC Environment studying environmental contaminants such as lead, mercury, PCBs and DDT and their impacts on human and environmental health.

During his time with Health Canada, Jay led the Human Health component of the federal Northern Contaminants Program, helping assess contaminant exposure in Arctic Canada and contributing to guidance for First Nations and Inuit communities on reducing exposure while safely maintaining traditional diets.

Jay also co-led the Human Health Assessment Group of the Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Program, working with scientists across the circumpolar region to better understand exposure to persistent organic pollutants. That work contributed scientific evidence used in the development of the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants.

A longtime member of both the federal and provincial Green parties, Jay has been active in election campaigns and environmental advocacy for decades. He has also participated in direct actions to protect old-growth forests in Temagami, Ontario and at Fairy Creek in British Columbia.

Jay is running in Courtenay-Comox to bring his experience in public health, environmental science and advocacy into public service and to help strengthen the connection between healthy communities and a healthy environment.

Name: Will Cole-Hamilton
Bio:
Will Cole-Hamilton: Standing firm for Courtenay-Comox

Will Cole-Hamilton is a strong advocate for the Comox Valley. As a former small business owner with a background in law, Will has been elected twice to Courtenay City Council and serves as Chair of the Comox Valley Regional District. He also led the creation of the Comox Valley Housing Authority which aims to build the affordable housing that people in the Comox Valley need to build good lives.

Will and his family live in Courtenay on the traditional territories of the K’ómoks First Nation. He knows that people in Courtenay-Comox need a government that is going to stand firm for them during this trade war.

Will Cole-Hamilton, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect the services that families need, and build the homes, infrastructure and economy we need for a stronger province.

Name: Bert Chen
Bio:
Bert Chen is a small business owner on Vancouver Island that is running to represent the Cowichan Valley and bring his experience with BC’s industrial sector and mill towns to Victoria.

A lifelong British Columbian, Bert grew up in a rural community where his family ran a small gas station and his first job was working behind the pump. Bert has seen the effect of our once strong resource economy diminished due to overly long permitting processes and knows that we need to grow BC’s economy by fast tracking projects to provide decent, stable jobs for hardworking British Columbians.

Throughout his career, he has worked in small remote communities across Canada, including BC and the North, including many where he was honoured to work with First Nations in developing critical infrastructure projects to support communities.

As the owner of a local Vancouver Island firm that provides project management and construction services for power plants and other large industries across Canada, he has worked to build clean power projects around the world, including those on Vancouver Island and the BC Coast.

Alongside his work, Bert has served with the Elks of Canada and the BC Elks Association as its long time finance director, helping to manage the charitable organization and its kids camps across the province.

In his leisure time, Bert and his wife enjoy sailing off Maple Bay.

Name: Justin Douglas
Bio:
Justin Douglas is a small-business owner, lawyer by training, and community advocate running to represent the Cowichan Valley. Raised on Vancouver Island by a single mother, Justin proudly calls the Cowichan Valley home and is committed to making sure local communities have a strong voice in the decisions that affect their lives.

Justin is the co-founder of EMBER Studios Duncan and VIT Management. As a local entrepreneur, he understands firsthand the realities of running a small business, creating opportunities, supporting workers, and contributing to the community.

He holds a degree in Political Science from the University of Victoria and degrees in both Common Law and Civil Law from McGill University. His legal and community experience includes work in immigration and refugee law, legal information services, restorative justice, and non-profit organizations.

Justin has also worked on community development initiatives involving ecotourism, infrastructure, access to safe drinking water, and youth engagement. His writing has addressed issues including the criminalization of poverty and the importance of including Indigenous legal perspectives in Canadian legal education.

Justin is running because he believes government should be accountable to the people it serves. His priorities include strengthening public services and social programs, protecting the environment, supporting a fair economy, and ensuring people across the Cowichan Valley are represented in the decisions that shape their future.

Name: Debra Toporowski
Bio:
Debra Toporowski is on your side in Cowichan Valley.

A member of the Cowichan Tribes, Debra Toporowski (Qwulti’stunaat) is a two term elected councillor in the municipality of North Cowichan and a five time councillor of Cowichan Tribes — the first elected woman in these communities to hold both positions on two councils at the same time. Born to a First Nations mother and Chinese father, Debra is a champion for Indigenous watersheds and the services people count on in the Cowichan Valley.

She knows people in the Cowichan Valley are facing the same big challenges so many people across BC are facing: housing, healthcare, and affordability. She and David Eby’s BC NDP team are on your side so we can keep building more housing, improving healthcare services, and making life more affordable.

Debra knows this government is looking out for people in Cowichan Valley. Under David Eby and the BC NDP this government is building a new Cowichan District hospital, a new Cowichan secondary school, while lowering ICBC costs for drivers, and increasing the minimum wage. You can count on them to fight for you and your family.

Name: Kuldeep Rangi
Bio:
Kuldeep Rangi is deeply connected to the Delta North community and has been actively involved in local organizations, sports, and community activities. His children are active in the community through hockey and soccer, while Kuldeep regularly participates in pickleball, tennis, and other activities with local residents.

Kuldeep is a successful business owner who operates a real estate marketing brokerage. He also brings nearly a decade of banking experience with Scotiabank and First West Credit Union, giving him valuable experience in business, finance, and working with families and local businesses.

Kuldeep is stepping forward because he believes Delta North deserves a strong local voice and practical leadership focused on the needs of the community.

Name: Monica Mohan
Bio:
Monica Mohan is the BC Conservative Party candidate for Delta North.

Monica is a practicing lawyer in British Columbia and a resident of North Delta. Born and raised in Vancouver, Monica grew up in an immigrant family, with her parents having roots in India and Fiji. In addition to English, Monica is fluent in Punjabi and Hindi. Her family background has shaped her appreciation for diverse communities and given her an understanding of the challenges families can encounter, including the barriers they may face as they build their lives in Canada.

She graduated with honours from Pennsylvania State University (Penn State) with a degree in Administration of Justice before pursuing her law degree in the United States, where she was awarded an academic scholarship. Her professional experience in law, public service, and community organizations has shaped her perspective on issues affecting individuals, families, and communities.

Before becoming a lawyer, Monica worked in civilian roles with the Vancouver Police Department and the Guelph Police Service, gaining firsthand exposure to the criminal justice system.

Monica is committed to access to justice, meaningful community engagement, and ensuring that people feel heard and understood when navigating public institutions and systems. Her professional and community experiences have reinforced her belief in the importance of public service, accountability, and practical solutions to the challenges facing individuals and families.

As a lawyer and community-minded professional, Monica brings a perspective grounded in legal experience, service, advocacy, and a desire to contribute meaningfully to her community.

Outside of her professional and community work, Monica enjoys spending time with her family and exploring local parks and outdoor spaces together.

Name: Todd Schierling
Bio:
Building a stronger economy and province for Delta North

Todd Schierling has spent his career keeping people safe. He is President of the BC Professional Firefighters’ Association and a Suppression Fire Captain with Surrey Fire Service, where he has served since 1996.

He also spends his off hours making his community stronger. A committed community volunteer, Todd helped launch the Surrey FF Goodwill Senior Girls High School Basketball Tournament in 2001, which has provided more than $125,000 in bursaries to female student-athletes.

Todd has also served on the BC Municipal Pension Plan, BC Federation of Labour Executive Council, BC First Responders Mental Health Committee, and on national academic working groups focused on firefighter cancer research and early detection.

Todd Schierling, David Eby and the BC NDP will stand up for families, protect people and the services they count on, and build a stronger economy and province, so that everyone can build a good life.

Name: Ian Paton
Bio:
Ian Paton is a lifelong resident of Delta South and a dedicated public servant, currently serving as the MLA for Delta South since 2017. He lives on his family farm in Delta with his wife, Pam.

Career

Ian has over 30 years of experience running and owning a dairy farm and farm auction business, which has provided him with extensive agricultural knowledge. He was elected as a Delta Councillor in 2010, where he chaired key committees such as the Agricultural Advisory Committee and the Dikes and Drainage Committee. As an MLA, Ian has served on the Select Standing Committees on Health and Agriculture, Fish and Food, and has been the Shadow Minister for Agriculture and Food.

Community Involvement

Ian is deeply involved in his community, having served as the past president of the East Delta Community Hall Society and as a volunteer firefighter with Hall 4. He has also contributed to various local organizations, including the Delta Hospital Foundation, REACH Child and Youth Development Society, and the Delta Farmland and Wildlife Trust.

Name: Jason McCormick
Bio:
Jason McCormick: On your side in Delta South.

Jason McCormick has fought for better public and active transportation for more than a decade. A bus driver for TransLink and community leader, Jason is extremely active in the BC cycling community and the South Delta Basketball Association, growing the latter to more than 400 youth participants.

Families in Delta South and across BC are facing real challenges, and Jason McCormick and the BC NDP are ready to take them on: building homes for people, strengthening our public healthcare system, and making day-to-day life more affordable.

Jason McCormick, David Eby and the BC NDP team are on your side and ready to take on the big challenges facing your community.

Name: Jim McMurtry
Bio:
Jim McMurtry was born and raised in Toronto, the son of a former Chief Justice of Ontario and Order of Canada recipient.

He is an award-winning teacher who gained renown for standing against the exploitation of schoolchildren for political advantage. Fired by the Abbotsford School District in 2023 for speaking honestly about residential schools, he has become a nationally recognized voice on the failure of Indigenous policy, the defamation of the dead in Canadian history, and the defence of fundamental Canadian values.

His professional résumé is impressive. He holds a Ph.D. in Educational Theory from the University of Toronto and has served as a teacher, principal, and college lecturer over four decades. He has been committed to a life of service at school as a coach, club supervisor, and organizer of events for students with disabilities.

In addition to his love for and commitment to teaching and his country, Jim has built a thriving family, including his wife, a retired vice-principal, his three children and their spouses, all of whom are lawyers, and his seven grandchildren who live nearby.

Jim has deep ties to the South Delta riding, where he resides with his wife and family.

Nobody who has met Jim can doubt his love for this province and this country. Jim is running to reaffirm all that is positive about our province and our country, and he is running to preserve British Columbia’s beautiful and glorious heritage.

Name: Sid Tobias
Bio:
Sid Tobias is a decorated Canadian Armed Forces veteran, experienced public servant, and municipal leader with deep roots in Esquimalt–Colwood.

Born in Esquimalt, Sid served nearly 25 years in the Canadian Armed Forces, much of that time based at CFB Esquimalt. His distinguished military career included receiving the Meritorious Service Medal for his role in integrating Canadian, NORAD, and U.S. forces in support of the 2010 Olympic Games. He also served as chair of a NATO working group.

Following his military service, Sid spent more than a decade working in the B.C. Public Service, bringing his experience in leadership, collaboration, and public administration to the provincial level.

In 2022, Sid was elected Mayor of View Royal and became a director with the Capital Regional District. As mayor, he has focused on practical, community-based solutions, including advancing View Royal’s first comprehensive Official Community Plan update since 2011, supporting efforts to establish a primary-care clinic for residents without a family doctor, and helping re-establish an ambulance station in the community.

At the regional level, Sid has worked to strengthen cooperation among municipalities, First Nations, regional governments, and other partners, including efforts surrounding the future of the E&N rail corridor.

Sid believes British Columbia needs stable, practical and collaborative government focused on delivering results rather than increasing political division. His priorities include housing, health care, transportation, infrastructure and affordability, with an emphasis on governments working together to address the challenges facing communities.

With decades of military, provincial and municipal public service, Sid brings extensive leadership experience and a lifelong commitment to serving the communities of Esquimalt–Colwood.

Sign up to stay informed and receive news from CentreBC:

Name: Dave Johnston
Bio:
Dave Johnston is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Esquimalt-Colwood.

The son of two public school teachers, Dave was born in Prince Rupert, raised in Campbell River, and now calls Colwood home. For the past decade, he has served in the Canadian Armed Forces as a Canadian Ranger.

After studying at Camosun College and living in Victoria for several years, Dave obtained his Red Seal as an electrician from BCIT and began working in BCs North at Mount Milligan. The Rio Tinto Alcan upgrade project then brought Dave to Kitimat, where he founded the nonprofit organization, The North Matters, to advocate for responsible resource development. For over three years, Dave worked with the Haisla Nation managing capital projects and assets.

Dave understands the issues facing both rural and urban communities in BC, and is eager to address the needs of Esquimalt-Colwood residents. An avid outdoors enthusiast, Dave enjoys hiking and camping with his three dogs: Boss, Apollo, and Loki. When not exploring the beaches and forests of the South Island, Dave can be found cooking up new recipes in his home kitchen and attending local events.

Name: Sidney Coles
Bio:
Sidney Coles is a journalist, communications professional, researcher, and former public servant running to represent Esquimalt-Colwood. Her career has focused on environmental justice, human rights, Indigenous issues, gender equity, and building stronger, more inclusive communities.

Based in Victoria, Sidney has worked as a freelance journalist since 2021, including two years as a Local Journalism Initiative reporter with Capital Daily. Her reporting has appeared in Ricochet Media, the Watershed Sentinel, Canada’s National Observer, the Toronto Star, the Hamilton Spectator, and Women and Climate, with a particular focus on climate change, environmental justice, and Indigenous land rights in British Columbia.

Sidney has also worked closely with Indigenous leadership in British Columbia. As External Communications Manager for the Gitanyow Hereditary Chiefs, she supported communications on land governance, resource development, and Indigenous rights. Earlier in her career, she worked internationally on climate and gender equity, including evaluating environmental grant-making across sub-Saharan Africa and advising on gender and resource governance initiatives.

Her public-service experience includes senior policy and program roles with the Ontario government. At the Ministry of Education, Sidney evaluated programs supporting Indigenous children and youth and children in care. At the Ministry of the Status of Women, she helped manage an employment program designed to reduce barriers facing Indigenous, racialized, and newcomer women entering skilled trades, technology, and entrepreneurship.

Sidney has also worked in humanitarian and international development settings, including with Doctors Without Borders in the Democratic Republic of Congo and on a psychosocial support initiative for refugee mothers and young children in Türkiye.

She holds two PhDs from the University of Toronto. She completed a PhD in Comparative Literature in 2008 and a PhD in Applied Psychology and Human Development in 2024, with research focused on women’s empowerment and the gendered impacts of mining in international development. Sidney was also nominated for a Rhodes Scholarship at McMaster University and held a Junior Fellowship at Massey College.

As a reporter in the Capital Regional District, Sidney has developed a close understanding of the challenges facing local municipalities and communities. She is running to bring that experience to public life with a focus on evidence-based policy, environmental responsibility, reconciliation, accountable government, and ensuring Esquimalt-Colwood remains a place where people and families can feel welcome, safe, and able to thrive.

Name: Darlene Rotchford
Bio:
Darlene Rotchford: building up a stronger Esquimalt-Colwood

Darlene Rotchford has been fighting for people for her entire career. Elected as the MLA for Esquimalt-Colwood in 2024, she proudly served as the Parliamentary Secretary for Armed Forces Development and Veterans’ Affairs.

Prior to provincial politics, as an elected councillor in Esquimalt, she’s fought for homes for people. And as President of the Victoria Labour Council, she took on powerful interests on behalf of working families, fighting for good wages and working conditions. In her professional life, she took on tough challenges in mental health and addictions, working to ensure people get the treatment they need so they can get well.

Darlene Rotchford, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for our province, protect people and services, and build a stronger economy, so you can build a good life in the community you love.

Name: Tony Luck
Bio:
About

Tony Luck is a dedicated leader, community advocate, and the Conservative Party of British Columbia MLA for Fraser-Nicola. Born and raised in British Columbia, Tony has a deep connection to the region and a passion for serving its residents. With a diverse background spanning finance, public service, and community engagement, Tony is committed to bringing positive change to Fraser-Nicola.

Proven Experience

Tony’s extensive career includes a decade as a financial planner, 26 years with BC Hydro, and his current role as a professional realtor. He has also served as a councillor on Mission City council and held leadership positions within the Fraser Valley Regional District and the Southern Interior Local Government Association (SILGA). Tony’s wealth of experience demonstrates his commitment to effective governance and community service.

Community Involvement

Tony is actively involved in various community organizations, including the Chamber of Commerce, Community Futures Nicola Valley, and the UFV Alumni Association. He believes in the power of grassroots initiatives to drive positive change and has dedicated his time to volunteering and supporting local causes. Tony’s community involvement reflects his deep-rooted commitment to the well-being of Fraser-Nicola residents.

Key Goals

Tony’s key goals for Fraser-Nicola center around transparency, accountability, and fiscal responsibility in government. He aims to implement fair taxation policies that support economic growth and alleviate the burden on working-class families. Additionally, Tony is a passionate advocate for affordable housing and healthcare reform, seeking practical solutions to address these pressing issues.
