Through engagement with medical professionals and community stakeholders, Tony aims to improve access to quality healthcare services for all residents of Fraser-Nicola.

With a proven track record of leadership, community involvement, and a commitment to addressing the needs of Fraser-Nicola residents, Tony Luck is serving as a strong voice in the BC Legislature.

Name: Patrick Michell
Bio:
Patrick Michell is the retired Chief of T’eqt”aqtn’mux (Kanaka Bar Indian Band) and a lifelong resident of the Fraser Canyon. His career spans law, Indigenous governance, renewable energy, economic development, community safety and climate resilience.

Patrick graduated from the Administrative Management program at Douglas College in 1989 and from the University of British Columbia’s law program in 1993. He began his professional career working on Aboriginal Fisheries Strategy agreements and later served as a Lands Officer with Indigenous and Northern Affairs Canada. After completing his legal articles, he practised law in Lytton from 1997 to 2005.

In 2005, Patrick shifted his focus toward community development and renewable energy. He became closely involved with the Kwoiek Hydro project, a renewable energy initiative first developed by Kanaka Bar Indian Band. He later served as Community Liaison, Lands and Economic Development Officer and, from 2015 to 2022, Chief of Kanaka Bar Indian Band.

During his time in leadership, Patrick also served in a number of advisory and director roles related to climate policy, clean energy, agriculture, finance, Indigenous health and economic development. These included appointments to the BC Climate Solutions Council, the BC Centre for Innovation and Clean Energy, the Fraser Basin Council, the BC Indigenous Advisory Council on Agriculture and the BC Real Estate Foundation.

His commitment to climate resilience is also deeply personal. Patrick and his family were evacuated during the 2021 Lytton fire and, like many people across the Fraser Canyon, experienced the displacement, infrastructure damage and repeated extreme weather that followed. From 2023 to 2025, he served as Rebuild Director for Lytton First Nations, focusing on rebuilding and strengthening community and regional resilience.

Today, Patrick continues to provide contracted services and speak publicly on climate change, resilience and community development. He believes the future of the Fraser-Nicola region depends on combining Indigenous knowledge, modern science and technology, strong local leadership and long-term investment in community safety.

Patrick is running to bring decades of experience in law, governance, renewable energy and climate resilience to the people of Fraser-Nicola and to help build communities that are safer, stronger and better prepared for the future.

Name: Mike Hicks
Bio:
Mike Hicks is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Juan de Fuca–Malahat

Mike has called this community home for 28 years, building businesses, raising his family and serving the people of the region. A graduate of BCIT’s Hotel Management program, Mike’s career has included forestry, tourism, hospitality and the recreational fishing industry. He has managed resorts and owned and operated fishing lodges in coastal communities including Hakai Pass, Sointula, Bamfield and Port Renfrew. Today, Mike and his wife Kathy operate Arbutus Cove Guesthouse in Sooke.

Mike’s commitment to his community led him into public service. For 13 years, he served as the elected Capital Regional District Director for the Juan de Fuca Electoral Area, representing East Sooke, Otter Point, Shirley, Jordan River, Port Renfrew, Malahat and Willis Point. During his time in office, Mike worked directly with residents, businesses, First Nations, community organizations and all levels of government to deliver practical results for the communities he represented.

His record includes advocating for the East Sooke Fire Hall, replacement of the Roche Cove Bridge, Highway 14 access from Gillespie Road, Sooke’s artificial turf field, the Charters River salmon hatchery, the Sooke Regional Library and the acquisition of important regional parkland. Mike also spearheaded efforts to improve cellular and emergency communications along Highway 14, helping bring seven new cellular towers to approximately 70 kilometres of the corridor.

As the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Juan de Fuca–Malahat, Mike brings decades of business experience, 13 years of elected public service and a deep understanding of the communities he seeks to represent. He is committed to listening to residents, standing up for rural and coastal communities, and working for practical solutions that make life more affordable, strengthen public safety and ensure government is accountable to the people it serves.

Name: David Evans
Bio:
David Evans is running to serve as MLA because he believes British Columbians deserve better representation and a government focused on improving people’s lives and strengthening their communities.

Born and raised on Vancouver Island by a mill-working father and a school trustee mother, David has deep roots in the region. He graduated from high school in Victoria before attending university in Toronto and later spending several years working in Vancouver.

David’s career has taken him through broadcasting, writing, community service, and entrepreneurship. In Vancouver, he worked in radio, freelanced for magazines, and served as Distribution Supervisor at the Vancouver Food Bank.

For most of the past four decades, David has been self-employed. He founded Victoria’s first Zero Impact landscaping company and later built a successful community hub, café, and bakery that employed up to 20 people across three locations before its operations were transferred to a community co-operative in 2023.

Today, David operates a retail and wholesale coffee roasting business in Sooke, where he has lived, farmed, gardened, and raised three daughters. His experience as a parent, small business owner, employer, and community member has given him a firsthand understanding of the pressures facing families, workers, and local businesses.

David believes government should serve people rather than powerful corporate interests. He is concerned about rising inequality, the loss of good-paying jobs, and the long-term sustainability of B.C.’s resources, and he is running to advocate for an economy and government that put communities first.

David holds an Applied Arts Degree from Toronto Metropolitan University. He previously ran as a BC Green candidate in the 2024 provincial election, finishing third in a historic outcome for BC Greens.

Name: Dana Lajeunesse
Bio:
Standing up for families in Juan de Fuca-Malahat

Elected MLA for Juan de Fuca-Malahat in 2024, Dana Lajeunesse has deep roots on southern Vancouver Island. He served as Parliamentary Secretary for Accessibility, he worked to advance accessibility and inclusion for people with disabilities across British Columbia.

A longtime resident of Sooke, he spent his childhood in Jordan River, expecting to grow up and work in the forestry industry, like his Dad and his Grandfather before him. Then, in 1989, a life-altering injury at work changed everything.

Unable to continue working in forestry, Dana went back to school. He earned a degree from Camosun College in Mechanical Engineering Technology, and worked in the industry for twenty four years. He built strong connections in his community, serving on the Mayor’s Advisory panel for economic development and Sooke Region Chamber’s Board of Directors. He was elected to the District of Sooke Council in 2019, and re-elected in 2022.

Dana Lajeunesse, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for our province, protect people and the services they count on, and build a stronger economy and province.

Name: Peter Milobar
Bio:
Peter Milobar is a dedicated Conservative MLA for Kamloops Centre with deep roots in the Kamloops community, where he lives with his wife Lianne and their three grown children. Together, they operate a local small business, reflecting their commitment to the local economy and community engagement. Peter’s longstanding connection to Kamloops is matched by his passion for public service and his active involvement in community life.

Career

Peter Milobar’s career in politics and public service spans over two decades, marked by significant roles and achievements. Elected MLA for Kamloops-North Thompson in 2017 and 2020, and current MLA for Kamloops Centre, elected in 2024. Most recently serving as Shadow Minister for Finance, Peter has a strong focus on fiscal responsibility and economic development. His previous roles include serving as Opposition House Leader and Shadow Minister for Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation, Environment and Climate Change. Before his provincial role, Peter was the Mayor of Kamloops for three terms, where he demonstrated leadership and commitment to local governance. He also served as chair of the Thompson Regional Hospital District for five terms and as a director for the Thompson-Nicola Regional District since 2005. His extensive experience extends to work with the BC Transit Board of Directors, PRIMECorp, and the Local Government Contract Management Committee.

Name: Ward Stamer
Bio:
About Ward

Ward Stamer, a devoted husband to his beloved wife Carleen and a proud father of two adult children and three grandchildren, has deep roots in Barriere, where he has called home since his youth. With a career spanning many years in the forest industry, Ward’s commitment to his community is unwavering.

Leadership and Community Involvement 

Ward’s dedication to public service began long before his mayoral tenure, serving as Chairman to the Barriere Improvement District, overseeing essential services such as solid waste management, streetlights, water, and fire services. His leadership continued as he was elected to Barriere’s first Council upon incorporation, eventually earning the trust of the community to serve as Mayor in 2018 and subsequently re-elected in 2022.

As a Lions Club member for over three decades, Ward embodies the motto “We Serve,” which reflects his lifelong dedication to his community and its people. During his two terms as Mayor, Ward has confronted the challenges faced by municipalities head-on, prioritizing critical issues such as healthcare access, affordable housing, and senior care.

Under Ward’s leadership, significant infrastructure improvements have been realized, including enhanced water system capacity and the expansion of the business and industrial park sectors, providing localized employment opportunities for residents.

Commitment to Kamloops-North Thompson

Healthcare Access: Ward advocates for streamlining accreditation processes to attract and retain medical professionals, ensuring residents have access to quality healthcare services.

Affordable Housing: Recognizing the housing affordability crisis, Ward proposes fostering public-private partnerships to unlock land for sustainable housing projects, coupled with strategic infrastructure investments.

Economic Stability: Ward prioritizes fiscal responsibility by curbing excessive spending, and conducting a comprehensive review of provincial taxes to alleviate burdens on residents and businesses.

New Initiatives: Ward is committed to revitalizing the local economy by promoting resource industries such as forestry, mining, agriculture, and tourism, thereby creating jobs and opportunities for families. Additionally, he envisions a future of energy self-sufficiency through investments in renewable energy sources.

Ward’s leadership, community involvement, and forward-thinking platform embody a vision of progress and prosperity for Kamloops-North Thompson. With his proven track record and unwavering dedication, Ward is poised to lead the region towards a brighter future for all its residents.

Name: Kristina Loewen
Bio:
Professional Experience

Kristina is a seasoned real estate professional, known for her exceptional ability to prioritize her clients’ needs while maintaining a level-headed approach under pressure. Her career has not only honed her skills in negotiation and client relations but has also given her a deep understanding of the local housing market.

Community Involvement

In addition to her work in real estate, Kristina has been actively involved in various aspects of the healthcare system. Starting as a care-aide, she later became a doula, supporting families during childbirth. Her commitment to empowering individuals extends to her role as a youth and young adult leader in her community, where she inspires others to achieve their goals.

Advocacy and Values

Kristina is a passionate advocate for affordable housing, recognizing the importance of stable and accessible housing for all. She is also committed to extensive tax reform and fiscal responsibility, believing that a balanced budget and a profitable economy are crucial for the prosperity of British Columbians.

Personal Life

Kristina Loewen has been an integral part of the Kelowna community for 25 years. She is happily married to Andrew, and together they have four children. Their enduring marriage of 26 years this spring is a testament to their commitment to family values.

Vision for the Future

Kristina envisions a future where individuals and families are empowered in all aspects of their lives, including health, finances, and relationships. She believes that a strong, safe, and united community, coupled with a thriving economy, are essential for achieving this vision. Kristina’s strong conservative values drive her commitment to forging a better future for Kelowna, the province, and all its residents.

Kristina Loewen’s blend of professional expertise, community engagement, and strong conservative values make her a strong MLA for Kelowna Centre. Her dedication to empowering individuals and families, coupled with her commitment to affordable housing and fiscal responsibility, positions her as an MLA who is ready to lead Kelowna into a prosperous future.

Name: Loyal Wooldridge
Bio:
Loyal Wooldridge: Building up Kelowna Centre

A successful entrepreneur, social equity advocate, Regional District of Central Okanagan Director and Former Chair, Loyal Wooldridge was elected as a Kelowna city councillor in 2018 and 2022. During the 2023 Grouse Complex fires, Loyal’s communication efforts kept thousands of evacuees and families informed during a devastating crisis, while helping secure vital disaster relief funding so communities can rebuild. Loyal is an active community volunteer with the YMCA, BC SPCA and KGH Foundation, among other organisations.

Loyal knows that housing, healthcare and affordability are big challenges across BC, and Kelowna Centre is no different. People here need a representative who will fight hard for them — building more housing that’s affordable, improving healthcare services and strengthening our resilience to climate-fueled fires and drought.

Loyal Wooldridge, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for British Columbians against external threats, protect the services people count on, and build for the future.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.

Name: Pavneet Singh
Bio:
Pavneet Singh is a successful entrepreneur, community advocate, and political leader who has called the Okanagan home for more than 25 years. Through his business ventures and community involvement, he has built strong relationships with residents, local businesses, first responders, and community organizations.

Pavneet currently serves as Vice-President of the Conservative Party of B.C., following his previous role as Director-at-Large. His leadership is rooted in entrepreneurship, community service, and a commitment to bringing people together.

During the 2024 provincial election, Pavneet chose not to run as an independent and instead supported the Conservative Party of B.C., putting the broader conservative movement ahead of his own political ambitions and helping avoid a split in the conservative vote.

As an entrepreneur, Pavneet has built and operated multiple businesses throughout the region. He has created employment opportunities and remains actively involved in the local business community.

Pavneet is also a strong supporter of firefighters, first responders, and community organizations, and continues to contribute his time and resources to causes that strengthen the community he has called home for more than two decades.

Name: Carter Mochinski
Bio:
Carter Mochinski is a youth advocate, climate organizer and community member who grew up in Lake Country and has a strong connection to the Okanagan. He is passionate about climate action, reducing inequality, improving education and making sure young people have a meaningful voice in public life.

Carter represented Canada as a delegate at the United Nations Climate Change Conference COP30 in Brazil, where he advocated for climate education and spoke about the impacts of climate change on young people. He has also worked with the BC Parks Foundation and independently to support stronger connections between nature, climate education and the provincial curriculum.

He is also a TEDx speaker and has spoken publicly about inequality in the education system, including the experiences of neurodivergent learners and the need for more inclusive approaches to learning.

Carter currently serves as Director of Research and Publications with the BC Youth Council, a non-partisan, youth-led organization focused on connecting young people with politics through educational resources, advocacy and opportunities to engage with elected representatives.

His community involvement also includes serving as a youth representative with the BC Parks Foundation and previously as a Youth Councillor with the District of Lake Country, where he advocated for young people in his community.

Having grown up in the Okanagan, Carter has a deep appreciation for the balance of natural beauty, urban communities and rural life that defines Kelowna-Lake Country-Coldstream. He is running to bring his experience in youth advocacy, climate action and education into public service and to be an accessible and engaged representative for the community.

Name: Alexandra Wright
Bio:
Candidate — Kelowna – Lake Country – Coldstream

Alexandra is a first-generation Canadian who was raised with a deep appreciation for the freedoms and opportunities that Canada provides, but also with the understanding that democracy can never be taken for granted. Good government depends on elected representatives who are accountable to the people they serve, and more importantly, upon the citizens who hold those representatives accountable.

Alexandra earned her BA in Anthropology from the University of Calgary before briefly moving to California, where she obtained her Juris Doctor degree from UCLA School of Law. After practising law for several years, Alexandra returned home to Canada and built a career as a legal advisor in the energy sector. In 2013, Alexandra and her husband, John, incorporated a full-service supply chain consulting firm. Over the years, they have grown their business while raising their daughter and running their family farm in Ellison, gaining firsthand experience of the challenges faced by farmers, parents and small business owners in our province.

Alexandra believes strongly in standing up for her community and in leading by example, and over the past years she has led rallies and campaigns within her region to oppose unlawful dumping, protect waterways and take a stand against irresponsible development that threatens to harm the future of the Okanagan Valley. Her favourite part of living in Ellison is listening to the owls hooting at night.

Alexandra believes British Columbians deserve leaders who approach public service with humility, make decisions openly and transparently, and never lose sight of the fact that a government only exists to serve its citizens. If elected, Alexandra will bring to the legislature the same approach that has guided her throughout her career: read the fine print, think critically, ask difficult questions, and never be afraid to challenge the status quo. Most importantly, she intends to remain true to the principles that brought her there in the first place.

Name: Gavin Dew
Bio:
Gavin Dew is a business leader, entrepreneur, and executive with extensive experience in governance and public policy. As the MLA in Kelowna-Mission and the Conservative Critic for Jobs, Economic Development, and Innovation (JEDI) & AI, Gavin is driven by a passion to renew and rebuild BC’s economic potential.

Personal Life

Born and raised in British Columbia, Gavin lives in Kelowna with his wife, Erin, and their two children, Abby and Evan. The Dew family is committed to building community through both volunteerism and small business. Erin, a UBC Forestry graduate, has a diverse background that includes working with children on the autism spectrum and running a small business. Together, they recently launched Play Area, Kelowna’s newest indoor playground, to serve the growing number of young families in the Okanagan.

Professional Background

Gavin’s career spans two decades at the intersection of business, public policy, and technology. He has played a key role in building public understanding and support for complex policies and projects across Canada, including affordable housing, energy infrastructure, and tech clusters. Most recently, Gavin served as Chief Strategy Officer for a $5 billion agricultural innovation and food security project in BC. He also has a strong academic background, with a BA from UBC and an MBA from the University of Oxford, where he focused on corporate social responsibility.

Community Involvement

Gavin is deeply committed to his community. Prior to being elected, he served on the boards of the Business Council of British Columbia and Resource Works, an organization promoting responsible resource development. He has also served in governance roles with organizations like UBC, Kwantlen Polytechnic University and Community Futures, a rural small business lender. Gavin continues to volunteer as chair of the Veterans Transition Network, a national mental health charity that played a crucial role in evacuating Afghan interpreters at risk from the Taliban. His community efforts have earned him recognition, including being named a “Forty Under 40” by Business in Vancouver for his leadership.

Name: Gordon Skulnec
Bio:
Gordon Skulnec is the Conservative Party of BC Candidate for Kootenay Central

Gordon is a husband, father, volunteer and small business owner. He and his wife were both born and raised in the West Kootenays and have been married for 19 years.

Gordon began his career as a medical radiographer at Kootenay Boundary Regional Hospital in Trail before joining the RCMP. He served 17 years as a general duty police officer in the East Kootenays, beginning in Cranbrook, and retired from the Kimberley detachment in May 2023. For the past 20 years, he has also run a small business as a rental housing provider and property manager, working with landlords and tenants alike, and for the past decade he has operated a business in Salmo.

Serving his community, especially its young people, has always been important to Gordon. He started as a youth group leader in Trail and coached Cranbrook Minor Baseball house and all-star teams for four years. Today he serves as Director of Baseball for the Cranbrook Minor Ball Association and drives the team bus for the Cranbrook Bandits. Faith matters deeply to his family. They attend Connect Church, where he helps lead the men’s group. 

Gordon brings a humble heart and a willingness to listen, and he is committed to working alongside the people of Kootenay Central to build real progress for their communities.

Name: Brittny Anderson
Bio:
Protecting the things that matter in Kootenay Central

Brittny Anderson is a lifelong resident of the Kootenays and former small-business owner. Elected as MLA for Nelson-Creston in 2020, and re-elected in 2024, Brittny has served as Minister of State for Local Governments and Rural Communities, Parliamentary Secretary for Tourism, as well as the Premier’s Special Advisor on Youth.

Brittny previously served her community as a Nelson city councillor and board member for the Regional District of Central Kootenay, where her work covered environmental services, resource recovery and water systems. Like so many people in the Kootenays, Brittny is passionate about spending time outdoors, and can often be found hiking with her family and her dogs Stella and Boreal.

Brittny Anderson, David Eby and the BC NDP are standing up for BC with a plan to fight for our province and country, protect people and services, and build a stronger economy.

The plan is working. We can’t stop now.

Name: Hunter Corrigal
Bio:
Hunter spent twenty years doing the jobs that keep B.C. running: fighting wildfires, securing our courts, working our mines and supporting kids in our classrooms.

He runs a small business and is raising two daughters. He has also engaged with our healthcare system through his cancer journey. Hunter knows where this province works and where it is letting people down, and he is running to be a part of the solution in making life better.

Hunter holds a Diploma in Tourism & Recreation Management from the College of the Rockies and a Sheriff Training Certificate from the Justice Institute of BC.

He is the owner-operator of an exploration logistics and hardscape company. In his community, he has served as past president of the Wildhorse Cycling Club and as a Special Olympics ski coach.

Hunter is running to fight for safer communities, resource jobs, strong schools, better healthcare and lower taxes.

Name: Warren Mirko
Bio:
Warren Mirko is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Kootenay-Monashee

Warren has more than 15 years of experience in public relations, crisis response, and risk management, having supported public protection mandates at BC Financial Services Authority, Engineers and Geoscientists BC, Transport Canada, and other regulatory authorities. His work has included regulatory reform, public safety issues, stakeholder disputes, and high-profile matters requiring coordination between government, industry, professionals, and affected communities. He holds a BA in Political Science from the University of British Columbia.

Warren’s work spans both the public and private sectors, where clear communication and public disclosure are critical to maintaining public trust. He is a Councillor in the Village of Warfield and a public affairs consultant who helps clients navigate government relations and align with regulatory and community expectations.

Warren contributes to media on issues of economics, governance, and accountability, bringing a candid perspective to land use and public policy in BC. He enjoys travelling throughout BC with his family and spending time outdoors. He also speaks Japanese and has practised Okinawan karate for more than 15 years.

Name: Connie Larochelle
Bio:
Connie holds a Master of Arts in Environment and Management from Royal Roads University and a Bachelor of Natural Resource Sciences from Thompson Rivers University. Her academic background includes environmental science, economics, statistics, cost-benefit analysis and Geographic Information Systems.

Her professional experience also includes work with business intelligence tools, including Power BI, and she was a finalist in the Institute of Public Administration of Canada’s Policy Pitch competition for work involving the use of business intelligence tools in the public service.

Connie is concerned about growing pressures on land, water and natural resources and how those pressures affect food security, housing and community health. She believes public policy should take a long-term approach to protecting the resources communities depend on while supporting people in their everyday lives.

Connie is running in Kootenay-Monashee to bring her experience in public service, environmental research and community advocacy into the Legislature, with a focus on sustainability, responsible resource management and practical solutions for local communities.

Name: Steve Morissette
Bio:
Taking action for you in Kootenay-Monashee.

Steve Morissette was the Mayor of Fruitvale, where he and his wife have raised four boys. First elected ten years ago, he has a record of action on housing and childcare, having led the building of a 37 seat daycare and a 31 unit fully accessible affordable housing complex. Under his leadership, Fruitvale committed to paying people good wages, and put a plan in place to move to 100% renewable energy by 2050.

Elected in 2024, Steve has brought his drive and record of action to the Legislature as MLA for Kootenay-Monashee. As a member of David Eby's BC NDP team, he's taking bold action to tackle the big challenges facing people in that riding: building homes for people, strengthening our public healthcare system, and helping with costs.

You can count on him to fight for you.

Name: Pete Davis
Bio:
Kootenay Roots and Upbringing 

Pete Davis hails from Revelstoke and was raised in Cranbrook, instilled with conservative values rooted in responsibility, tradition, individual freedom, and service. Married to Heather since 2002, they are proud parents to four children and are dedicated to their life in the Kootenay region of British Columbia. Pete is an avid outdoorsman with strong ties to the motorcycle, boating and camping communities.

Balancing the responsibilities of work and raising a family, while being a dedicated husband, has instilled in him a strong sense of empathy, compassion, and commitment to serving others. During his childhood years Pete’s family faced significant economic hardships. Raised by a loving and hard-working single mother, he remembers what it feels like to wonder where the next meal would come from and if rent would be made. These early experiences have prepared him to represent constituents with compassion, integrity, diligence, and a deep-seated commitment to positive change.

Professional Experience

Pete’s extensive experience as a business professional has allowed him to cultivate strong and enduring relationships with key stakeholders across various sectors critical to the economy of the Elk Valley and East Kootenays. These sectors include logging, forestry, automotive, heavy equipment, and mining, each playing a vital role in the region’s economic vitality and the livelihoods of countless working families.

Through his interactions and collaborations with industry leaders, workers, and community representatives, Pete has gained a deep understanding of the challenges and opportunities faced by these sectors. He is acutely aware of the regulatory, economic, and environmental factors that impact businesses and workers alike.

Pete’s belief in the hard-working families of Kootenay-Rockies is unwavering. He recognizes the resilience and dedication of these families who rely on these industries for their employment and economic stability. As a consistent voice in Victoria, Pete is committed to advocating for policies and initiatives that support the growth and sustainability of these sectors, ensuring that working families have the opportunities and resources they need to thrive.

Vision

Pete is committed to challenging failed policies and advocating for change in Victoria. His love for Canada and British Columbia fuels his dedication to serving the people and ensuring their voices are heard in government. Pete Davis is a strong, consistent voice that the Kootenay-Rockies need in Victoria.

Name: AJ Wolfe
Bio:
AJ has more than 25 years of construction experience, mostly in the Kootenay region. He has worked on residential, commercial, industrial, and civil projects as a tradesperson, superintendent, and project manager.

People often call AJ when a project has a difficult problem to solve. Whether the challenge is building a reliable estimate, sorting out procurement, or finding a simpler, more cost-effective way to do the work, he digs into the details and finds a practical path forward. He leads from the front, gets his boots dirty, and takes responsibility for results.

AJ is committed to conservative values: individual responsibility, responsible spending, and respect for the rights of citizens. He believes rules and constitutional principles must mean something in practice. Leaders should follow the rules they ask others to follow, keep their commitments, and remain accountable to the people they serve.

He is running to represent the people of Kootenay–Rockies and help build a government that listens to all British Columbians, tackles hard problems, and follows through.

Name: Kim Lockhart
Bio:
Kim Lockhart is a community leader, nonprofit executive, small business owner, and mother of five who lives with her family in Qualicum Beach on Vancouver Island.

Kim is the Founder and Executive Director of Butterfly Support Network, a registered Canadian charity supporting individuals and families navigating infertility, pregnancy loss, and infant loss. What began as a grassroots community initiative in 2019 has grown under her leadership into a provincial organization delivering programs, education, advocacy, and community support across British Columbia. Her work has given her extensive experience in nonprofit leadership, governance, fundraising, program development, and working alongside families, healthcare professionals, and community partners to improve systems of care.

Prior to her work in the nonprofit sector, Kim worked in education and developed a particular passion for special education, inclusion, and disability rights. As a parent with children in the public school system, she also understands firsthand many of the pressures facing families, educators, and schools in British Columbia.

Kim chose to run because she believes many British Columbians no longer feel politically represented by the choices available to them. She sees CentreBC as an opportunity to build a balanced middle, bringing people together around strong public services, fiscally responsible government, economic growth, socially inclusive values, and a commitment to improving healthcare and mental health supports across our province.

Above all, Kim hopes to be a strong local voice for the people who call Ladysmith and Oceanside home, listening to constituents, understanding the issues affecting their everyday lives, and ensuring their concerns are represented in Victoria.

Name: Kris McNichol
Bio:
Kris McNichol is the BC Conservative candidate for Ladysmith-Oceanside.

Kris and his wife, Sheryl, have made their home in the Parksville and Nanoose Bay area for more than 30 years. They raised three daughters in the community and are now grandparents.

For the past 25 years, Kris and Sheryl have built and run CPI Equipment, a Nanoose Bay-based pumps, piping and water systems business serving homes, farms and aquaculture operations across the region. Growing the company from the ground up has given Kris a firsthand understanding of what it takes to meet a payroll, cut through red tape and keep good jobs in the community.

Kris has spent as much time giving back as he has building his business. He coaches the Rage softball team, serves as president of the Oceanside Minor Softball Association, and previously led the Sproat Lake Water Sports Association. He is also a volunteer firefighter.

Kris ran for the federal Conservatives in Courtenay-Alberni in 2025, an experience that sharpened his sense of the challenges families across the Island face: the rising cost of housing and everyday life, strain on the healthcare system, worsening public safety, and a regulatory burden that makes it harder to run a business. He’s running provincially with the same message: government spending needs to be accountable, and leadership needs to focus on results.

Name: Stephanie Higginson
Bio:
On your side in Ladysmith-Oceanside.

Twice-elected to the Nanaimo-Ladysmith Board of Education, Stephanie Higginson is also a past president of the BC School Trustees’ Association.

She and her family have lived in the Ladysmith-Oceanside area since 2010, where she and her husband raise their two children on a small farm in Cedar. She knows that families in BC need strong public services, and a government that’s dedicated to making life easier. Stephanie knows that BC is strong when our public services are strong.

Stephanie, David Eby and the BC NDP are on your side, delivering strong public services, good jobs, and a strong and clean economy. You can count on them to work hard for you.

Name: Sean Flynn
Bio:
Sean Flynn is the CentreBC candidate for Langford-Highlands.

A longtime Langford resident, husband and father of three, Sean understands the pressures facing families across the West Shore, from rising housing and living costs to strained infrastructure and the challenge of building a secure future in British Columbia.

Sean served for 13 years in the Royal Canadian Navy as a Naval Warfare Officer. His military career developed a practical approach to leadership grounded in service, accountability and making difficult decisions under pressure.

After leaving the Navy, Sean worked as a Senior Technical Trainer with Lockheed Martin Canada. He subsequently entered the capital-markets sector and now holds senior leadership positions with Canadian public companies, serving as Chief Executive Officer and a director of Avventura Resources Ltd. and as Chief Operating Officer and a director of Planet Green Metals Inc. He is also Head of Project Management with Mid Atlantic Capital Associates Ltd.

Through these roles, Sean has gained direct experience managing organizations, raising capital, working within complex regulatory systems and confronting the real-world challenges faced by businesses trying to operate and grow in British Columbia.

Sean believes government must remember that it serves the public not the other way around. He is running to bring disciplined, practical leadership to the Legislature and to advocate for responsible public finances, a stronger economy, attainable housing and essential services that keep pace with the West Shore’s rapid growth.

He joined CentreBC because he believes British Columbians deserve a pragmatic alternative: economically responsible, socially inclusive and focused on delivering results rather than deepening political divisions.

Name: Cindy Scott
Bio:
Cindy Scott is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Langford–Highlands.

A community builder, Langford business owner and woman in the trades, Cindy has built her life around family, hard work, and a deep connection to her community. For more than two decades, Cindy has owned and operated KC Custom Designs Ltd., a Langford-based home building and renovation company. Her experience in construction and business has shaped a practical approach to leadership– focused on problem-solving, sound decision-making, and accountability.

Cindy and her husband of 32 years, a local firefighter, have raised their family with a strong appreciation for service, responsibility, and giving back. Her role as a mother and grandmother has also influenced how she thinks about the opportunities and quality of life being created for the next generation.

Giving back has always been an important part of Cindy’s connection to the community. She created The Holiday Home Tour at Bear Mountain, which ran for five years, with 100% of the proceeds going to vital community services, including The Goldstream Food Bank.

Cindy believes meaningful representation begins with listening. Her campaign takes a grassroots, community-focused approach, centered on staying connected to the people of Langford–Highlands and understanding the issues that affect their families and businesses. Her priorities include greater government accountability, improved access to healthcare, making life more affordable, and strengthening public safety. Cindy is committed to practical solutions that reflect the needs and priorities of the people she hopes to represent.

Name: Christopher Moon
Bio:
Christopher Moon is a public servant, union supporter and longtime Vancouver Island resident who has lived in Langford with his husband and two dogs since 2021. Born and raised in Victoria, he cares deeply about the future of the West Shore and British Columbia’s coastal environment.

Christopher has more than nine years of experience with the Ministry of Forests and BC Wildfire Service, where he has worked in financial administration, payroll and team leadership in a complex, fast-moving emergency-services environment. He has progressed from an entry-level clerical role to Provincial Payroll Lead and is experienced in working under pressure, managing complex systems and supporting diverse teams.

While working full-time with BC Wildfire, Christopher earned a Diploma in Public Administration from Camosun College. His leadership has also been recognized with a BC Wildfire Service Emerging Leader Award.

The rising cost of housing, groceries and everyday necessities is a major reason Christopher decided to run. He believes government should prioritize accessible public services, economic security for working people and long-term planning over short-term solutions.

Christopher is also concerned about political division and the spread of misinformation. He believes people should be able to work together even when they disagree and that public service should remain focused on practical solutions for the communities government represents.

Christopher is running in Langford-Highlands to bring his experience in public administration, emergency services and team leadership to the Legislature, with a focus on affordability, strong public services and responsible environmental stewardship.

Name: Ravi Parmar
Bio:
Ravi Parmar: Fighting for people in Langford-Highlands

Ravi Parmar was elected as an MLA in 2023, and was the youngest representative in the 43rd Legislative Assembly. He has a long record of standing up for people, and getting results.

In government, he served as Minister of Forests, standing on the front line as the country grappled with Donald Trump’s attacks on our forest industry. Prior to provincial politics, he was Chair of the Sooke School Board, where he worked with John Horgan and the BC NDP government to deliver the largest expansion of public schools in the district’s history.

In the 2024 election, Ravi Parmar and David Eby committed to build a new secondary school in north Langford - and they have delivered. Construction is set to begin in 2027 on a new 2,000 seat school - the largest investment in education the community has ever seen.

The BC Conservatives might be ready to cozy up to Trump and cut the services you count on. But Ravi Parmar, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan: stand up for BC and Canada, protect what matters, and build a strong economy, independent of the United States.

The plan is showing results. We need to keep going.

Name: Harman Bhangu
Bio:
Harman Bhangu is the MLA for Langley–Abbotsford and serves as the BC Conservative Shadow Minister for Transportation. First elected to the Legislative Assembly in 2024, he is a strong advocate for working families, economic growth, public safety, and the industries that have helped build British Columbia.

Before being elected to the Legislature, Harman helped rebuild the Conservative Party of British Columbia. Elected Vice-President at the party’s 2022 Annual General Meeting, he also served as Regional Director for Surrey. That same year, he ran as the Conservative candidate in the Surrey South by-election, helping re-establish the party’s presence and increasing its support to nearly 13 percent in just three weeks.

Raised in a hardworking family, Harman developed a deep appreciation for the people who keep the province moving. His family has deep roots in trucking, aggregate hauling, road building, construction, and forestry. His father worked in trucking, mills, and industrial jobs across British Columbia, giving Harman firsthand insight into the importance of resource industries, transportation, skilled trades, and the men and women who build the province. Those experiences continue to shape his commitment to protecting family-supporting jobs.

In the Legislature, Harman has been a vocal advocate for improving transportation infrastructure, reducing barriers to investment, supporting responsible resource development, and restoring affordability for British Columbians. He regularly speaks on issues affecting workers, small businesses, agriculture, and economic growth.

Outside the Legislature, Harman is actively involved in his community, attending local events, supporting service organizations, and meeting with residents, businesses, and community leaders across Langley and Abbotsford. He believes effective representation begins with listening and ensuring local voices are heard in Victoria.

Harman remains committed to practical solutions that create jobs, strengthen communities, and grow British Columbia’s economy.

Name: Misty Van Popta
Bio:
Deeply Rooted in Langley

Misty is a Langley native, having grown up and raised her two daughters in various parts of the community. Her lifelong connection to Langley fuels her passion for advocating and serving its residents. From her early years, she’s been actively involved, and served as a Municipal Councillor for the Township of Langley.

Leadership and Community Focus

Elected in 2022 as part of the ‘Contract With Langley’ team alongside Mayor Eric Woodward, Misty brings a strong focus on community engagement. She actively contributes on regional boards like Metro Vancouver’s Water Committee and previously served on their Climate Action Committee. Misty‘s past roles include the Township’s Heritage Advisory Committee, the Langley Christian School Society, and the Fort Langley Business Association.

Building a Strong Community

Beyond her political role, Misty is a seasoned project management professional in construction. Her education from SFU and PMP designation make her a valuable asset. She actively contributes to building much-needed housing and possesses a deep understanding of urban planning challenges, financial implications, and risks associated with housing development. Misty‘s prior experience as a small business owner and in the pharmaceutical software industry further broadens her perspective.

Driven to Serve

A proven leader and high achiever, her top priority is serving her community, family, and friends. As a Councillor, she’s known for her logical approach, thoughtful consideration, and long-term vision. Overcrowding in schools, a lack of investment in health care, no investment in transit or transportation, and provincial legislation that has negatively impacted the community inspired Misty to put her name forward for the 2024 election and win.

Name: Holly Isaac
Bio:
Building BC strong in Langley-Walnut Grove

Holly is no stranger to fighting for people. As the 1st Vice-President of the local executive of the Canadian Union of Postal Workers, she served as the local media contact during their time on the picket lines, and she has served on the regional disciplinary committee.

Born in Surrey and raised in Langley, Holly grew up in the riding of Langley Township-Fraser Heights. Her family has lived in North Langley for 32 years, where she’s happy being surrounded by the rich history, beautiful mountains, and incredible farms and one of a kind restaurants and cafes. When she isn’t working, Holly loves to sing, read, cross-stitch, and spend time with her dog, Zoey.

Holly Isaac, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to build a stronger province - by creating jobs, strengthening healthcare, and making life more affordable.

Name: Jody Toor
Bio:
Leading Holistic Healthcare in Langley-Willowbrook

As a dedicated community servant and advocate for holistic health care, we are proud to have Jody Toor as our MLA for Langley-Willowbrook. Born in Langley, Jody has deep roots in the community and has been running her own integrative holistic clinic in Langley.

In addition to her professional work, Jody is a devoted mother to her two beautiful daughters Nya & Jaya wife to Dr. Charn Toor who has his Optometry clinic in Walnut Grove, balancing the demands of family life with passion for helping others.

Jody Toor holds a double PhD in Doctor of Integrative Medicine and Doctor of Humanitarian Services with the Board Of Integrative Medicine, non-prescribing and is not registered with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of British Columbia. Jody’s academic achievements, have provided her with a strong foundation in healthcare, mental health, social services, and advocacy. dedicated to using this knowledge and expertise to address the complex challenges facing our community and to promote policies that support the health and well-being of all individuals.

As a breast cancer survivor, Jody has  experienced firsthand the physical, emotional, and financial toll that serious illness can take on individuals and their families. This personal journey has deepened her commitment to advocating for comprehensive healthcare policies that prioritize prevention, early detection, and holistic approaches to wellness.

With a strong background in healthcare, and personal health journey, community service, and academic achievement, Jody is ready to bring her unique perspective and dedication to public office.

In her role as a community worker with local food banks, and different charity groups, she has witnessed the impact of health disparities and the importance of access to nutritious food in promoting overall well-being. This experience has reinforced her belief in the interconnectedness of health, social justice, and community support.

As your Conservative Party of BC MLA for Langley-Willowbrook, Jody believes that her unique combination of personal experience, professional expertise, and community involvement, positions her to be a strong advocate for healthcare reform and social justice. Jody is committed to championing policies that prioritize the well-being of all individuals, especially those facing health challenges and other adversities. Jody is excited about the opportunity to serve her community and to work towards a more inclusive, healthier and common sense future for all.

Name: Shubham Joshi
Bio:
For over 20 years, my life’s work has been about listening, caring, and helping people thrive. As a long-time resident, a registered physiotherapist, and a Clinical Instructor in the Faculty of Medicine at UBC, I’ve dedicated my career to public service, health advocacy, and education. My journey has always been guided by a profound desire to give back to the community that has given my family so much. Now, I am stepping forward to bring those exact values of gratitude and service to Victoria as your Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) in the upcoming provincial election on Saturday, October 24, 2026.

As a university educator, I have the privilege of teaching and mentoring students in the Master of Physical Therapy program at UBC. It’s a role that demands deep institutional knowledge, trust, and a commitment to strong family values—the very principles of hard work, mutual respect, and community care that my family and I hold dear. Beyond the classroom and clinic, my commitment to giving back to society is woven into my daily life. Whether I am supporting my son’s local soccer team, spearheading vital community projects, or collaborating within our diverse local social and community networks, I believe that building a stronger province starts with being actively engaged right here at home.

In my clinical practice and community work, I sit down with ordinary people every single day. Because I am on the ground, I understand the complex, interconnected systems driving the real pressures facing our local families. True public service requires both a compassionate heart and a knowledgeable, evidence-based approach to governance. For an everyday family, it isn’t about big political debates—it’s about practical solutions to counter the rising cost of groceries under historic inflation, policy reforms to address the skyrocketing cost of housing, and strategic investments to alleviate the stress of gridlock because our regional infrastructure and transit connectivity haven’t kept pace with our community’s rapid growth.

My journey has allowed me to care for patients at every level, from local moms, dads, and grandparents to elite athletes on the world stage as a National Team Physiotherapist. Speaking English, Hindi, Gujarati, and Punjabi allows me to connect with the beautiful, vibrant fabric of our community, ensuring every family and local entrepreneur has a voice.

I am running for MLA because I want to ensure that our community remains a safe, affordable, and vibrant place to raise a family and grow a business. I will bring the heart of a caregiver, the analytical knowledge of a clinician, and the accountability of an educator to the legislature to look out for you. Let’s work together to build a healthier, stronger, and more equitable future for our families. This October 24, I ask for your support to build a better British Columbia.

Name: Lawrence Mok
Bio:
About Lawrence:

Elected as Conservative MLA for Maple Ridge East in 2024, Dr. Lawrence Mok, together with his wife and two young children, moved to Canada from Singapore in 1988. He and his family have lived in Maple Ridge for over 30 years, where he enjoys the outdoor life, including the Golden Ears Mountains, glacier lakes, and beautiful rivers. In his spare time, Lawrence likes to go for walks on the river dykes, go cycling, visit friends, or relax with a good book.

Education and Memberships:

Lawrence attended universities in both Canada and America, earning nine degrees, including a Bachelor of Applied Science & Technology, Bachelor of Electrical Engineering, Master of Business Administration, Master of Arts in Religion, Master of Divinity, Master of Theology, Doctor of Religious Studies, Doctor of Business Administration, and Doctor of Philosophy in Business Administration.

He is a Life Member of The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (USA), a Fellow Member of The Institution of Engineering and Technology (UK), a Fellow Member of The Chartered Management Institute (UK), and an Associate Member of the Evangelical Theological Society (USA). Additionally, Lawrence is a Registered Applied Science Technologist (British Columbia, Canada), a Registered Incorporated Engineer (UK), and a Chartered Manager (UK).

Professional Experience:

Lawrence has over 30 years of experience in the manufacturing, installation, sales, and services of overhead cranes, crane components, and hoists in British Columbia, serving industries such as manufacturing, steel production, sawmills, lumber mills, steel and stone & marble warehouses, construction, mining, oil & gas, recycling, and water and waste treatment plants. He also conducts overhead crane operator safety training seminars. Lawrence has also taught business management courses as a guest lecturer at universities in Canada, China, and North Africa, and he preaches part-time at several local churches.

Community Involvement:

Lawrence has been an active volunteer at the Maple Ridge Salvation Army Church, serving in various capacities over the years. His dedication to community service reflects his commitment to addressing local issues and improving the quality of life for all residents.

Political Vision:

When Lawrence first moved to Maple Ridge 35 years ago, it was a quiet town. Over the past two decades, Maple Ridge and Mission have grown rapidly, bringing challenges such as homelessness, poverty, drugs, long wait times at hospital emergency departments, rising crime rates, and a lack of recreational facilities and employment opportunities.

As a longtime resident of Maple Ridge, Lawrence understands the needs and aspirations of Maple Ridge and Mission residents.

In addition, Lawrence supports the Conservative Party of BC’s common-sense approach to scrapping the carbon tax, building pipelines, lowering taxes, balancing the budget, cracking down on violent crime, and reducing wait times for medical treatment. MLA Lawrence Mok is leveraging his extensive experience and skills to serve the residents of Maple Ridge East effectively.

Name: Daniel Kite
Bio:
Daniel Kite is a public school teacher, union advocate and Maple Ridge resident who has spent the past several years working with students, colleagues and families in the community. He currently teaches Social Studies, English and Student Leadership in School District 42.

Daniel holds a Bachelor of Arts (Honours) in English and Political Science and a Bachelor of Education from the University of Toronto, where he graduated with high distinction. Before returning to Canada, he spent seven years teaching internationally in China, Egypt and Russia, experiences that strengthened his belief in the importance of building connections across cultures and communities.

After moving to Pitt Meadows in 2020, Daniel began working with School District 42. In his first year in the district, he taught with Katzie First Nation before moving into elementary and secondary school settings. He has lived in Maple Ridge since 2023.

Daniel has also been active with the Maple Ridge Teachers’ Association, serving as a staff representative, participating in staff committees and supporting social justice work within the union. He has taken part in British Columbia Teachers’ Federation events and, in 2024, participated in the Teachers Institute on Canadian Parliamentary Democracy.

As a father of a young child with another on the way, Daniel is focused on the long-term future of families in British Columbia. His priorities include affordability, stronger care systems, support for workers and communities and an energy and industrial strategy that considers both people and the environment.

Daniel is running in Maple Ridge East to bring his experience in education, community leadership and advocacy into public service and to work toward long-term solutions for the challenges facing families and communities across the province.

Name: Hudson Campbell
Bio:
Building a stronger Maple Ridge East

Hudson Campbell is a School Trustee for School District 42, but his community involvement began long before that.

He was a founding member of UPlan with the City of Maple Ridge, served as President of the Maple Ridge Climate Hub, and was Director of Protocol for the 2024 BC Summer Games. Growing up attending local schools, he also chaired the District Student Advisory Council.

Hudson knows government choices directly shape the lives of British Colombians, from public education and health care to creating good jobs here in BC.

He is running to be a strong voice for his neighbours in Maple Ridge East, and to build a sustainable community where every senior, young person, and family can afford to live, work and build a good life.

Hudson Campbell, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to create jobs, strengthen healthcare and make life more affordable.

Name: Jordan Simmons
Bio:
Jordan Simmons is the co-founder and CEO of Nominee, a global technology platform and social enterprise empowering and equipping governments, political organizations and aspiring leaders with professional development and mentorship in governance, public policy and political leadership. He’s worked with elected officials, public institutions and NGOs around the world to promote and defend democracy and civic engagement while reimagining political leadership to solve the most pressing challenges of our time.

A leader in the tech sector for more than a decade, Jordan has worked for organizations ranging from multinational corporations to early-stage startups. Previously, he served as a senior advisor to several BC cabinet ministers, including the Minister of Community, Sport and Cultural Development, and the Minister of State for Seniors.

Sign up to stay informed and receive news from CentreBC:

Name: Doug Morneau
Bio:
Doug Morneau is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Maple Ridge-Pitt Meadows.

Doug has lived in Maple Ridge for eight years with his wife, Heather. They have three adult children and five grandchildren. Faith, family and community service guide everything Doug does, and he and Heather train together three mornings a week in strength training and Olympic weightlifting.

Doug knows how public money gets spent, and how to ask whether it is being spent well. He served on the board of BC Assessment, the agency that sets the property values local taxes are based on, where he sat on the Finance, Policy and Planning, and Human Resources committees and advised on technology and IT initiatives.

Doug brings four decades of business experience, building and running companies and advising organizations including Bell Media, BCAA, Lafarge, On Side Restoration and the Independent Wood Processors Association of BC. Today he helps companies find out whether their technology spending delivers results, and what to fix when it does not.

Name: Lisa Beare
Bio:
Lisa Beare: Building for the future in Maple Ridge-Pitt Meadows

Lisa Beare knows that British Columbians need a government that is willing to stand up for them. A mother to a young daughter, Lisa knows the challenges that families face first-hand, and she’s determined to take action to make life easier for them. That means investing in the services that families in Maple Ridge-Pitt Meadows rely on, like building new schools and increasing access to healthcare.

Lisa has been fighting for people for over a decade. She got her start in politics in 2014 as a school board trustee. After being elected to the provincial government in 2017, 2020 and 2024, Lisa has served as a Cabinet Minister with portfolios including tourism, culture, sport and post-secondary education.

The BC Conservatives might want to cut services and cozy up to Trump, but Lisa Beare, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan: to stand up for British Columbia, protect the services that families need, and build the infrastructure and economy we need for the future.

The plan is working. We can’t stop now.

Name: Susan Einarsson
Bio:
Born in Vancouver, Susan is an experienced communications professional, educator and broadcast media specialist with more than a decade of teaching experience at the British Columbia Institute of Technology (BCIT), complemented by twenty-five years working as a news anchor and reporter. She is knowledgeable about the political history of BC. Susan has served on the local board of the Federal Conservative Party and assisted with political communications in several campaigns.

Susan worked for CKNW/CFMI and News 1130, as a talk show host for CJME Regina, as a TV producer and as a CBC National Arts Reporter. She is experienced in public speaking, political grassroots organization, fundraising and community engagement.

Known for her no-nonsense, straightforward, friendly personality, Susan’s goal is to listen to the voters and act on their behalf to bring back common sense to political decision-making. Susan owns My Town Maple Ridge News Society, a local news organization sharing local stories on Facebook and YouTube. She is a writer, singer, painter and grandmother.

Susan is proud to be a OneBC candidate for Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows.

Name: Joshua Dahling
Bio:
Joshua Dahling’s path to public service has been shaped by lived experience, recovery, leadership and nearly three decades of helping others. He is running to represent Mid Island–Pacific Rim in Victoria. 

Born in Johannesburg, South Africa, Josh came to Canada in 1980 at the age of four. Growing up, he experienced extreme poverty, instability, homelessness and addiction. In 1997, he committed himself to sobriety, a decision that changed the direction of his life.

A year later, Josh left the logging industry and moved to Nanaimo to study human services. While raising three young children as a single father, he worked in alcohol and drug treatment facilities, gaining firsthand professional experience in addiction, mental health and recovery.

In 2009, Josh and his wife, Dr. Heather Mohan, began building what would become LUMARA, a registered Canadian charity supporting children, families and communities affected by serious illness, grief and bereavement. He has since helped lead multidisciplinary teams, develop innovative approaches to bereavement care, and train professionals and organizations across Canada and around the world.

Throughout his career, Josh has served on advisory committees and worked with governments on mental health, substance use and community supports, alongside families, frontline professionals, organizations and First Nations communities across the country.

Josh made Port Alberni home in 2018, drawn by the community and its incredible access to nature. When he’s not working, you’ll likely find him hiking, fishing, boating or swimming, no matter how cold the water is.

Name: Gracie MacDonald
Bio:
Gracie MacDonald is an educator, community leader and nonprofit executive with a strong background in public education, food security, affordable housing and community development.

She currently serves as Executive Director of a community school society on Denman Island, where she helps deliver recreation and educational programming for children and adults, as well as essential food programs including the island’s food bank.

Gracie also serves on the board of a nonprofit organization working to create affordable housing on Denman Island, bringing her commitment to practical, community-based solutions to one of the region’s most pressing challenges.

Her professional experience includes serving as an elementary school principal and teaching students from Kindergarten through Grade 12 on Vancouver Island. Before beginning her career in education, Gracie worked as a journalist and was a partner in a successful organic food business.

Gracie holds a Master of Education from the University of Victoria and an undergraduate degree from Concordia University. She is running in Mid Island-Pacific Rim to bring her experience in education, nonprofit leadership, food security and affordable housing into public service.

Name: Josie Osborne
Bio:
An experienced champion for Mid Island-Pacific Rim

Josie Osborne has called Tofino home for over 25 years, first moving there to work as a fisheries biologist for the Nuu-chah-nulth Tribal Council then leading an environmental education non-profit organization before serving as mayor of Tofino for almost eight years.

She was elected MLA for Mid Island-Pacific Rim in 2020 and 2024. She has served in five different portfolios, including Minister of Energy, Mines and Low Carbon Innovation and Minister of Health.

Josie has always worked hard to protect people and the services they value, whether that’s affordable housing, or improving access to health care, or making life more affordable. She’s a champion for sustainable resource development that builds strong local economies, and has always worked closely with local governments, First Nations, community organizations and employers to address challenges facing communities across her riding.

Josie Osborne, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect people, and build a stronger and more resilient economy.

Name: Mark MacDonald
Bio:
Mark MacDonald is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Nanaimo-Gabriola Island.

For more than 20 years, Mark has run his own successful publishing and communications companies. With his wife Lise, he published five editions of the Business Examiner covering most of British Columbia, and wrote columns on business, economic and political issues. Together they own and operate Communication Ink Media & Public Relations Ltd. Mark also served as Managing Editor of the Nanaimo Daily News.

Mark has long been a leader in his community. As President of the Greater Nanaimo Chamber of Commerce, he guided his team to be named BC Chamber of the Year in 2003. Today he serves as President of the Vancouver Island Junior Hockey League.

An award-winning writer, Mark is the author of It Worked For Them, It Will Work For Me: The 8 Secrets of Small Business I Learned From Successful Friends , which Dr. Peter Legge called a “must read” for business people of all ages.

Mark will bring that same practical, results-focused approach to Victoria, working to grow the local economy, support small business and deliver for the people of Nanaimo-Gabriola Island.

Name: Anna Mary McKenzie
Bio:
Anna Mary McKenzie (she/her) is a Cree journalist, policy advisor, child and youth advocate, and mother who has made her home in the Nanaimo community for many years. A proud member of Opaskwayak Cree Nation, Anna has strong ties to Snuneymuxw First Nation and is the mother of a Snuneymuxw child.

Anna’s advocacy is deeply connected to her own family and community. As the daughter of a day school survivor, she has spoken publicly about the intergenerational impacts of residential and day schools.

As a journalist, Anna has reported on issues affecting communities across British Columbia, with particular attention to Indigenous peoples, families, and maternal health. Her investigation into the province’s use of birth alerts contributed to broader public scrutiny, policy changes, and a class action lawsuit concerning the practice. Her community reporting has also been recognized with a Jack Webster Award.

Anna holds a Bachelor of Arts in First Nations and Indigenous Studies from the University of British Columbia and serves on the board of tâpwêwin media. Locally, she has helped organize community gatherings and advocated for pedestrian safety, including organizing a delegation to Nanaimo City Council following collisions along Departure Bay Road.

Anna is running to bring her experience in journalism, policy, advocacy, and community organizing to the Legislature and to ensure the people of Nanaimo-Gabriola Island are heard in the decisions that affect their families and communities.

Name: Sheila Malcolmson
Bio:
Sheila Malcolmson: Protecting what matters in Nanaimo-Ladysmith

Elected four times by her community, Sheila Malcolmson has been fighting for her community for years. As a past Member of Parliament for Nanaimo-Ladysmith, she served as the Minister of Social Development and Poverty Reduction in government.

She’s been part of the BC NDP team that’s delivering on David Eby’s plan to protect people - connecting more people to a family doctor, recruiting doctors and nurses from the US, bringing down housing costs and building up our economy and creating jobs.

Where the BC Conservatives would roll over to Trump and cut healthcare and education, Sheila Malcolmson, David Eby have a plan to stand up for BC and protect what matters.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.

Name: Kelsey Pringle
Bio:
Kelsey Pringle is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Nanaimo-Lantzville.

A Vancouver Island entrepreneur, business owner and community leader, Kelsey is a wife and mother of two who spent 12 years living in the Nanaimo-Lantzville area. At 36, she knows the pressures working families face because she lives them.

In the summer of 2026, Kelsey’s husband suffered a heart attack. Her family suddenly experienced the healthcare system not as a policy debate, but as patients waiting for urgent answers. Although Nanaimo Regional General Hospital serves Central and North Vancouver Island, Nanaimo patients needing cardiac catheterization must be transferred to Victoria, and Island Health’s own review has flagged the delays that creates.

That experience made healthcare a defining issue for Kelsey. She believes a growing region of hundreds of thousands deserves advanced care, including cardiac care, closer to home, and that no family should face delays in an emergency because of where they live.

Kelsey is the co-founder and owner of Motivation Monday Marketing, a digital marketing agency serving businesses across British Columbia. As an employer, she knows what it takes to meet payroll and create jobs. She sits on the Board of the Vancouver Island Economic Alliance, where she has seen that healthcare infrastructure is also economic infrastructure: communities need reliable services to attract families, workers and investment. She also co-founded Empower Women Canada, supporting women in business.

Name: George Anderson
Bio:
Taking action for you in Nanaimo-Lantzville.

Born and raised in Nanaimo, George Anderson is a commercial lawyer, a volunteer, and the youngest person ever elected to Nanaimo City Council.

He has served as Chair of the Vancouver Island University Board of Governors, and volunteered with the Canadian Bar Association’s Access to Justice Committee, Literacy Central Vancouver Island, the Nanaimo-Ladysmith Public Schools Foundation, among many other organization dedicated to making his community stronger.

His dedication to community service earned him the distinction for citizenship from the Nanaimo Chamber of Commerce, as well as the BC Achievement Award from the Lieutenant-Governor of BC in 2016.

George has an unwavering commitment to fairness and community development. He is taking action so people in Nanaimo-Lantzville can build good lives.

Name: Diane Black
Bio:
Diane Black is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Nechako Lakes.

Diane is a 3rd generation rancher with a deep respect for the generations who have gone before. She carries forward the grit, stewardship, and community commitment that built the region.

Her vision for Nechako Lakes is a region where those working hard to build a life for their families can have safe, affordable housing, clean air and water, and stable employment that doesn’t require relocation from our communities.

As the great granddaughter of Vanderhoof’s first doctor, Diane holds firm that health care should be delivered in the north, for the north and by the north. She is committed to improving health and social services so residents can rely on timely, high-quality care close to home.

A Chartered Professional Accountant, with an MBA, Diane brings experience across the agriculture, energy, logging, transportation and advanced education sectors. In her capacity as Associate Vice President Finance for Nicola Valley Institute of Technology, she secured major funding and successfully led projects including the Trades Building, the Mobile Trades Training Trailers and the Center of Excellence in Sustainability Buildings. These projects expanded training opportunities in Merritt and across British Columbia.

Diane is a lifelong learner and sees education as a critical driver for quality of life in our region. She recognizes the dedicated work of the teachers, administrators and support staff in each of our communities that strive together to build the future generation. As a mother of 3, Diane will be a strong advocate for education and long-term wellbeing of families throughout the Nechako Lakes region.

Name: Jesse Gervais
Bio:
Jesse Gervais: Building a stronger Nechako Lakes

Jesse Gervais works for the Municipality of Fraser Lake and serves on the boards of UNBC and the Fraser Lake Community Foundation. He has spent years working in economic development, helping create good local jobs and build stronger communities.

He is deeply involved in his community and passionate about making Nechako Lakes a great place to live, work and raise a family.

Jesse Gervais, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect the services that matter to people, and build a stronger economy and a stronger province.

The plan is working. We can’t stop now.

Name: Michele Lau
Bio:
Michele Lau is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for New Westminster-Coquitlam.

Michele Lau is an accomplished financial services executive and entrepreneur with more than 20 years of experience in banking, corporate finance, and private business leadership.

Following her banking career, Michele transitioned into entrepreneurship and financial advisory, founding and leading ventures in hospitality, real estate, and investment management. Her combined experience in institutional finance and private enterprise provides a strategic perspective on capital allocation, risk oversight, and sustainable business growth.

Michele is co-founder of the World Trade Centre Okanagan, the 8th licensed centre in Canada. With 300+ centres in over 100 countries, it connects Canada’s dynamic regions to global markets.

Michele holds a Bachelor of Commerce from the University of British Columbia and an Executive MBA from Simon Fraser University. She is an active community leader, a participant with the Vancouver Board of Trade and on the board of the Vancouver College Parent Association, where she leads fundraising and community engagement initiatives.

Name: Maureen Curran
Bio:
Maureen Curran is a scientist, educator, mother, and longtime community advocate who believes better is possible for British Columbia. She is running to help build a future where public investment strengthens communities, families can afford to thrive, young people have access to good jobs, and decisions are guided by evidence and long-term thinking.

She has spent nearly three decades working in British Columbia’s public education system. For 25 years, she has taught Science and Mathematics in Coquitlam, helping generations of students develop the critical-thinking skills needed to navigate a changing world. She also spent four years with Simon Fraser University’s teacher education program, mentoring future educators and helping build creative, sustainable, and inclusive learning communities.

At an early age, Maureen developed a love of science, the natural world, and community service. While raising her two sons in New Westminster, she has remained deeply involved in her community. She has coached Little League, organized fundraising for an accessible playground, participated in cycling advocacy, supported school clubs and extracurricular activities, and contributed to local organizations including New West Environmental Partners and the Climate Action HUB.

Maureen earned a Bachelor of Science from McGill University before moving to Victoria to complete a Master’s degree in Physics at the University of Victoria, later conducting research in nuclear physics at TRIUMF on the UBC campus.

Her scientific background and experience as a parent and educator shaped her commitment to environmental action. From 2019 to 2023, she participated alongside peaceful land defenders working to protect forest corridors and salmon-bearing streams affected by a proposed pipeline expansion.

Recognizing the role local governments can play in addressing climate change, Maureen helped bring activists from communities across British Columbia together to create the Climate Safe Cities Coalition. The initiative grew from a campaign supporting the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty into a province-wide effort working with municipal councils on policies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

Maureen is running to advocate for stronger public services, affordable housing, support for families and small businesses, environmental stewardship, and investments that build resilient communities for the next generation.
