Her entrepreneurial journey has not only emphasized the importance of fiscal responsibility but has also provided her with ample opportunities for high levels of community engagement.

Public Service and City Council Experience

In addition to her private sector experience, Claire Rattée has devoted four years of service to the Kitimat City Council. In this role, she played a pivotal part in advocating for policies supporting economic growth, community development, healthcare services, and affordable housing. Claire’s focus during her time on City Council was to represent struggling business owners, provide younger voters with representation, and enhance the quality of life for Northern B.C. residents. Notably, Claire made history as the youngest female ever elected to a council position in Kitimat.

Political Engagement and Federal Elections

No stranger to the political arena, Claire transitioned from City Council to run in the 2019 and 2021 federal elections. Despite an unsuccessful bid, she garnered considerable momentum within the Conservative Party. Under her leadership, the Conservative vote share increased from 24% to 36%, highlighting her ability to resonate with voters and fortify support for conservative principles in challenging territories.

Passions and Advocacy

Claire Rattée’s passions lie in economic development, addressing the housing crisis, and advocating for healthcare and addiction recovery support for her region. Her commitment to these crucial issues stems from a genuine desire to improve the lives of Skeena residents. Notably, during her tenure on City Council, Claire played a pivotal role in collaborative efforts leading to a positive final investment decision for the LNG Canada project, the largest private sector investment in Canadian history. This accomplishment underscores her ability to work collaboratively to achieve meaningful and lasting outcomes.

Conservative Vision for Skeena

As an MLA, Claire Rattée seeks to represent Skeena with conviction, aiming to preserve the principles that make the region strong and vibrant. She pledges to be a tireless advocate for cherished values and a steadfast voice for the community. Claire is dedicated to bringing common-sense conservatism to Skeena, making her an ideal to serve as a representative in the Legislature with an unwavering commitment to shared values.

Name: Nick Gottlieb
Bio:
Nick Gottlieb is a writer, researcher, community organizer, and PhD candidate at Simon Fraser University. His priorities for the change we need are shaped by his research into corporate power and his experience organizing in communities across British Columbia. He is running to advocate for greater investment in healthcare, housing, affordability, workers, and a liveable future, while challenging what he sees as excessive corporate influence over public policy.

For Nick, research and community organizing go hand in hand. While living in Squamish, he helped found the Squamish Resilience Network and co-led a campaign supporting the community’s “Just Recovery” initiative. Since moving to Terrace, where he has lived for the past five years, he has helped establish the Skeena Local Action Network and has been involved in campaigns focused on housing affordability, environmental protection, international solidarity, and proposed data centre development in the region.

His research focuses on the political economy of Canada’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) industry, including corporate influence on government, regional economic development, and the role of LNG in a changing global economy. In 2025, he was awarded a Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship.

Nick’s writing and journalism have appeared in Canada’s National Observer, the Vancouver Sun, Business in Vancouver, and other publications, and he is a regular columnist with Canadian Dimension. He has also published reports based on his research and presented his work to universities, community groups, and grassroots organizers.

He has also contributed his technical expertise to environmental and community initiatives, including the UBC Big Tree Registry and forestry advocacy projects. He serves on the board of BC Whitewater, a non-profit organization advocating for public access to free-flowing rivers.

Outside of his research and organizing work, Nick is an outdoorsman and award-winning photographer who spends much of his free time exploring the mountains and rivers of British Columbia. He is running to bring his experience as a researcher, writer, and grassroots organizer to be a committed champion for the people of the Skeena region, who deserve to believe in better.

Name: Sarah Zimmerman
Bio:
Sarah Zimmerman: Standing firm for people and families in Skeena

Sarah Zimmerman is an elected Terrace City Councillor, former journalist, senior communications leader, and fierce advocate for people and communities in the Skeena region.

She has spent more than two decades bringing the Skeena region’s residents together to work collaboratively on the issues that matter to them. Outside her professional commitments, Sarah volunteers her time to numerous organizations, such as the Terrace Rotary Club and My Mountain Co-op.

She will bring a unique understanding of the Northwest to Victoria. You can count on her to fight to protect the services that matter to people in the Skeena region, and build for the future.

Where the BC Conservatives would cut the services you count on and surrender to Trump, Sarah Zimmerman, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for people in British Columbia, protect the services that people count on, and build a stronger economy.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.

Name: Raman Sharma
Bio:
Raman Sharma is a long-time Surrey resident, entrepreneur, and community leader with more than 28 years of experience in Canada. Since arriving in Canada in 1998, he has built strong relationships throughout Surrey and British Columbia through business, construction, community service, cultural organizations, and civic engagement.

In 2016, Raman founded the Tradesman Association of BC and continues to serve as its President. Through the organization, he has created educational and professional opportunities for builders and tradespeople, including builder licensing preparation, energy advisor education, safety training, professional development, and networking.

Raman also founded and leads the Annual Construction Expo, bringing together thousands of builders, tradespeople, businesses, and community members. He is the founder of the South Asian Construction Excellence (SACE) Awards, recognizing achievement, professionalism, and excellence within the construction industry.

Through his education and community initiatives, Raman has helped hundreds of aspiring and working construction professionals strengthen their qualifications, expand their knowledge, and advance their careers in British Columbia. His work has also created opportunities for small businesses, tradespeople, and community members to connect, learn, and grow.

Raman believes that public leadership is about listening to people, understanding community needs, bringing people together, and turning ideas into practical action.

Name: Zeeshan Wahla
Bio:
Zeeshan Wahla is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey City Centre. 

Zeeshan is a Professional Engineer and small business owner who runs his own engineering consulting firm. Registered as a P.Eng. in four provinces, he brings extensive experience in engineering and planning, along with a professional commitment to honesty, integrity and protecting public safety and the environment.

Zeeshan arrived in British Columbia as an immigrant in 2007 and has proudly called Surrey home ever since. Raised in a family that valued hard work and perseverance, he pursued higher education and built a business of his own. That journey has given him a firsthand understanding of the pressures facing working families, from the rising cost of living to the challenge of getting ahead in today’s economy.

Zeeshan and his wife are raising their four daughters in Surrey, where they share their home with his mother. Providing his daughters with a good education and the opportunity for a bright future is at the heart of everything he does, and he wants every family in Surrey to have that same opportunity.

Name: Amna Shah
Bio:
Committed to Surrey City Centre.

Amna Shah has called Surrey home for nearly 20 years. Growing up, her family taught her about the importance of compassion, public service, and standing up for your community — values that guide her every day.

Like so many people in Surrey, Amna is concerned about housing. It’s what drove her to work with BC’s Ministry of Housing, where she helped move forward affordable housing policies and projects — many of which have become law and are in effect today.

Because she believes that no family should be left behind without enough to eat, she became a dedicated volunteer at the Surrey Food Bank, where she now serves on the Board of Directors. In this role, she’s helped expand distribution services across Surrey, helping to make sure that people and families using the food bank can get the nutritious food they need in a supportive, dignified environment.

Amna is focused on the issues that matter to people and families in Surrey, like expanded transit, strengthening education, building more healthcare facilities and keeping communities safe. Even better — she knows how to get things done.

You can count on her and David Eby to always have your best interests at heart.

Name: Bhandol Parm
Bio:
Bhandol Parm has been a resident of Surrey North for more than 10 years, and is proud to serve the community as a HandyDART operator.

Bhandol holds a BSc and MSc in Mathematics, bringing a practical, analytical, and evidence-based approach to the issues facing Surrey North.

Every day, Bhandol works alongside seniors, people with disabilities, families, and residents from all walks of life. Through local sports and community involvement, he also connects with young people and understands how important it is to give youth meaningful opportunities to learn, grow, and succeed.

Living and working in Surrey North for more than a decade has given Bhandol firsthand insight into the challenges Surrey North faces. He brings a genuine commitment to listening to people and finding practical solutions that work.

Bhandol’s priorities are clear: better public transit, stronger local infrastructure, more opportunities for youth, and accessible representation for everyone in Surrey North.

Bhandol’s goal is to be a strong voice for our community in Victoria—bringing the concerns, ideas, and priorities of Surrey North directly to the provincial government.

Name: Mandeep Dhaliwal
Bio:
Mandeep Dhaliwal’s journey to becoming the Conservative Party of BC MLA for Surrey North is a testament to his diverse experiences and unwavering commitment to community service. Migrating to Canada in his 20s with his family, Mandeep embarked on a path that blends his love for social services, entrepreneurial spirit, and passion for public engagement.

Family and Background

Raised in Surrey, Mandeep is a devoted family man, nurturing his small family, which includes his wife Pawan, a dedicated Registered Nurse, and their son Diltaj. His roots in social service sprouted in India, where he completed his Bachelor of Arts degree in group humanity and excelled in the folk game of Punjab, Kabaddi (wrestling). As a national-level player, he secured a gold medal in an inter-college tournament, reflecting his dedication and prowess in sports.

Entrepreneurship in Canada

Transitioning to Canada, Mandeep became a small business owner, establishing Fixman Auto Glass Repair and Fixman Auto Glass Supplier in Surrey. Through hard work and determination, he transformed his ventures into trusted brands within the industry. As a successful entrepreneur, Mandeep is attuned to the challenges faced by small businesses and is committed to advocating for policies fostering growth and supporting startups.

Community Engagement

Beyond business, Mandeep is deeply immersed in his local community. Actively participating in various events and initiatives, he supports local charities and organizations, embodying his belief in giving back to the community that supported his business.

Sikh Motorcycle Club and Philanthropy

Mandeep’s commitment to social services continues through his membership in the BC Sikh Motorcycle Club, engaging in rides that contribute to the community. Notable among these is the 2016 motorcycle ride from BC to Ontario, where he played a pivotal role in raising $100,000 for the BC Cancer Society. Another remarkable feat is his participation in a fundraising bike ride from Canada to India, setting a world record and generating $100,000 for the Khalsa Aid organization.

Advocacy and Vision for BC

Throughout his life, Mandeep has displayed a passion for public service, social justice, equality, and sustainability. His vision for BC focuses on critical areas such as affordable housing, education, healthcare, and environmental sustainability. Mandeep believes that by investing in these areas, a stronger, more inclusive community can be forged.

Community-Centric Representation

As an MLA, Mandeep is dedicated to listening to the concerns and ideas of community members, ensuring their voices shape the decision-making process. With experience, passion, and dedication, he envisions progress, opportunity, and a better future for all residents. Mandeep Dhaliwal is poised to be a dynamic representative, committed to transparency, accountability, and integrity in his role as a public servant.

Name: Sahib Thind
Bio:
Building a stronger Surrey.

Sahib Thind is the founder and president of the Professor Mohan Singh Memorial Foundation, which has advocated for recognition of the Komagata Maru tragedy and organizes the annual Mela Gadri Babiyan Da at Bear Creek Park. He is a fearless advocate for human and civil rights.

He received B.C.’s Medal of Good Citizenship in 2017. A Surrey North resident for more than 40 years, he is semi-retired and worked in the construction industry.

Sahib Thind, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to build BC strong: creating jobs, strengthening healthcare, and bringing down costs.

Name: Tanya Gupta
Bio:
Tanya Gupta is a business owner and Notary Public in British Columbia, bringing years of experience working directly with individuals, families, professionals, financial institutions, and businesses.

Since 2019, Tanya has owned and operated Tanya Gupta Notary Corporation, while also managing and operating SSTG Gas Station. Through her businesses, she has gained firsthand experience with the responsibilities and challenges of running a business, including managing employees, finances, customers, regulatory requirements, and day-to-day operations.

Tanya holds a Master of Applied Legal Studies from Simon Fraser University and a Bachelor of Computer Applications. Her professional and business experience has developed strong skills in leadership, communication, problem-solving, decision-making, organization, and working with people from diverse backgrounds.

Tanya is passionate about bringing her practical experience and community-focused perspective to public service. She believes that years of working directly with people, operating businesses, and serving clients have given her valuable insight into the responsibilities that come with serving the public.

Tanya Gupta is proud to be the OneBC candidate for Surrey North.

Name: Megan Knight
Bio:
Megan Knight has called the White Rock area home for more than 46 years. She graduated from Semiahmoo Secondary, went on to study at the University of British Columbia, and in 1998 was commissioned as a British Columbia Notary Public, establishing a practice she ran for 25 years, serving local families and businesses with integrity and dedication.

Megan’s commitment to her community led her into public service. She was first elected to White Rock City Council in 2014, serving as a Councillor until 2018, and was elected Mayor of White Rock in 2022. As Mayor, she has worked to keep White Rock safe, support local businesses, protect its natural spaces and ensure the city’s public spaces remain vibrant and welcoming for residents and visitors alike.

Her leadership extends well beyond city hall. Megan has served on the Metro Vancouver Board of Directors and the TransLink Mayors’ Council, giving her firsthand experience with the regional decisions that shape transportation, growth and costs for South Surrey and White Rock families. She has also served on the boards of the Sources Foundation, the Society of Notaries Public of BC, the Notary Foundation, the Fraser Valley Regional Library and Tour de White Rock. 

In 2022, Megan was honoured with the Queen Elizabeth II Platinum Jubilee Medallion in recognition of her contributions to community service.

As MLA for Surrey South, Megan will be a strong voice for safer communities and lower costs, and will deliver a provincial government that listens to the people it serves.

Name: Brent Chapman
Bio: MLA for Surrey South

Name: Nicholas Cartmell
Bio:
Nicholas Cartmell is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey-Cloverdale.

Nicholas is a brand strategist and community sport builder who has spent his career creating moments that matter to people. He and his wife, Leslie, have made Surrey home since 2012. They are raising a young son who plays competitive minor hockey, and two adult sons now building careers in engineering and the Canadian Armed Forces Reserves.

Community work has been the constant. As CEO of the BC Sports Hall of Fame and Museum, Nicholas led a non-profit accountable to a 23-member board and expanded a youth education program that reaches classrooms across British Columbia. He raised the funding for the Hall’s Indigenous Sport Gallery and led the effort to bring it online, so the stories of 40 First Nations and Métis athletes, coaches and builders could reach every corner of the province. He chaired business and community engagement for the 102nd Grey Cup Festival in Vancouver, and from 2016 to 2018 served on Capilano University’s Board of Governors, where he chaired the Investment Committee. Today he is Vice President of the Surrey 2027 55+ BC Games Host Society, preparing to welcome thousands of participants and visitors to Surrey next September.

Nicholas brings two decades of business leadership. Over 14 years at TELUS, most recently as Senior Director, Strategic Initiatives, Partnerships and Government Relations, he led national teams and budgets and negotiated $51 million in partnerships and investments. He went on to run the Western Canadian division of Canada’s largest event rental company, employing more than 100 British Columbians through peak seasons.

Name: Pat McCutcheon
Bio:
Pat McCutcheon is a retired professional engineer, small-business owner and longtime Cloverdale resident who raised his two sons in the community with his wife. He has seen firsthand how pressures on healthcare, public education, housing affordability and the environment affect local families.

Pat graduated from the University of British Columbia with a Bachelor of Applied Science and went on to build a long career in engineering. In 1995, he founded his own engineering consulting firm, providing services to heavy equipment manufacturers across the Lower Mainland. He operated the business for 28 years.

His professional background has given him experience in problem-solving, long-term planning and working with businesses across the region. Pat is also an active member of the Cloverdale District Chamber of Commerce.

He joined the BC Greens in 2019, motivated by a belief in evidence-based policy and the need for environmental, economic, social and fiscal sustainability.

Pat is running in Surrey-Cloverdale to advocate for stronger public services, more affordable housing, climate action and a more proactive approach to the challenges facing the community.

Name: Stephen Dooley
Bio:
Building a stronger Surrey-Cloverdale

Stephen Dooley is the BC NDP Candidate in Surrey Cloverdale. He is the recently retired Executive Director of the Surrey Simon Fraser University campus, and the former Director and Chair of the Surrey Board of Trade, as well as the Co-Chair of the Surrey Poverty Reduction Coalition. He also served as the co-chair of the Surrey Social Innovation Summit. In his various roles, Stephen has worked extensively with First Nations communities south of the Fraser River.

Prior to joining SFU Stephen taught criminology and sociology at Kwantlen Polytechnic University and he was the first Director of Community Engagement. He is known for his ability to build trust, bring diverse interests together, and turn shared priorities into action. He has extensive experience in public accountability, strategic planning, financial stewardship, and a longstanding commitment to accessible education, poverty reduction, youth opportunity, public safety, economic development, reconciliation, and community well-being.

Steve holds a Master’s degree in Sociology and a Bachelor’s degree in Sociology and History. He and his wife Preet have lived in the region for over 25 years. Their son Dave, daughter-in-law Jasmine and grandson Wilson are proud residents of Surrey Cloverdale.

Stephen Dooley, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to build BC strong: to create jobs, to strengthen healthcare, and to bring down the cost of living.

Name: Paul Brar
Bio: Paul Brar came to Canada in 1983 and began his working life as a shingle sawyer in Mission, BC. He built a career in real estate over the four decades that followed, and graduated from the University of British Columbia with a diploma in Urban Land Economics in 1999. Before coming to Canada, he attended DAV College in Jalandhar and Punjab Agricultural University in Ludhiana.

Name: Garry Purewal
Bio:
Garry Purewal is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey-Fleetwood.

Garry’s commitment to service began in uniform. As a Military Police member with the Canadian Armed Forces, he learned the discipline, integrity and sense of duty that have guided him ever since. That experience gave him a firsthand understanding of public safety and of what it takes to keep communities secure.x

After his military service, Garry built a career in business, owning and managing companies including a property restoration business. Running his own business has taught him what every small business owner in British Columbia knows: how hard it is to meet a payroll, keep costs down and grow when government makes it more expensive to do business every year.

Garry has also given his time to the next generation as a leader in youth sports, and has been active in community advocacy and political engagement, working with neighbours and local organizations on the issues that matter most to families.

That experience has given Garry a clear view of the challenges facing families, business owners and communities, and a strong commitment to public safety, responsible government, economic opportunity and effective public policy.

Name: Jagrup Brar
Bio:
Jagrup Brar: Building up Surrey-Fleetwood

Jagrup Brar has represented people in Surrey for decades. As the past Executive Director of the Surrey Self Employment and Entrepreneur Development Society (SEEDS), Jagrup trained new entrepreneurs to develop and launch successful small businesses — strengthening the community in which he, his wife and his two children live.

Jagrup is committed to building up Surrey, whether that’s a new hospital, or a SkyTrain extension, or a stronger economy with good-paying jobs, or homes - all the things people need to build a good life in the place they love.

The conservative parties would cozy up to Trump, cut healthcare, and hike costs on working people.

Jagrup Brar, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to lower costs, hire more healthcare workers, and build a stronger economy.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.

Name: Carolyn Hofbauer
Bio:
Carolyn Hofbauer grew up in Surrey’s Newton neighbourhood and attended Frank Hurt Secondary School. Surrey is where she went to school, built her career, and is raising her family.

Carolyn began working at 15 while continuing her education. After high school, she attended what is now Kwantlen Polytechnic University, where she studied music, English, and history. During her college years, she also worked as a substitute teacher.

Much of Carolyn’s early career was spent in the restaurant industry. She worked as a chef at Fresgo Inn before becoming head chef at The Vault Restaurant in Cloverdale, where she spent nearly a decade. The work demanded responsibility, teamwork, and the ability to listen to people.

Carolyn later joined her family business. Today, she manages BC Firearms Academy alongside her husband. Running a small business has given her firsthand experience with the challenges facing employers, employees, and families in British Columbia.

Carolyn and her husband are raising their son, Blake. Family is at the centre of her life and shapes how she thinks about the future of her community.

Carolyn’s involvement in politics began during college. Since then, she has volunteered on campaigns, knocked on doors, made calls, worked in campaign offices, and spoken with voters about the issues that matter to them.

Carolyn is running for OneBC to bring her experience as a mother, small business owner, and lifelong Surrey resident to provincial politics. She wants to represent the community she has always called home.

Name: Garry Thind
Bio:
Garry Thind is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey-Guilford.

Garry has proudly called Surrey home for more than 27 years, living, working, raising his family and serving his community in the city. For the past 12 years, he has served Surrey families as a Trustee on the Surrey School Board, where he is currently Vice-Chair, representing the interests of parents, students and the broader community.

Since 2014, Garry has taken on leadership roles across the school district, chairing committees including the Learning Liaison Committee, Traditional Schools, District Principal Selection, Secondary Vice-Principal Selection, the ELL Consortium and the Budget Committee. That work has given him extensive experience in governance, policy development and accountability, and in working collaboratively with parents, educators and community stakeholders. He also sits on the External Advisory Board of Western Community College in Surrey.

Garry’s commitment to Surrey extends well beyond the School Board. He is a past President of the Rotary Club of Surrey and currently leads the BC region for the Pingalwara Society of Ontario, a charitable organization. Since 2002, he has helped raise more than $5.4 million for charitable and community causes.

Professionally, Garry brings more than 14 years of management experience and more than 13 years in sales and marketing. He is currently a full-time Realtor with Century 21 Coastal Realty in Surrey, work that has sharpened his skills in leadership, communication and relationship-building.

Name: Garry Begg
Bio:
On your side in Surrey-Guildford.

Garry Begg knows the importance of giving families, kids, and schools the tools they need to succeed — now and later in life. Prior to being elected as the MLA for Surrey-Guildford in 2017, 2020 and 2024, he served in progressive law enforcement leadership with the RCMP for nearly 40 years where he gained a deep understanding of issues facing people living in Surrey.

Garry knows that Surrey is the fastest growing — and soon to be largest — city in BC, which comes with its own set of challenges for people who live here. It’s why he’s focused on ensuring the people of Surrey have the housing, education and health care support they need to build a good life here.

You can count on Garry Begg, David Eby and the BC NDP to look out for you and your family.

Name: Harman Preet Singh
Bio:
Harman Preet Singh is a legal professional with experience in criminal defence, immigration, administrative law, public policy, governance, technology, and business. He brings a unique combination of legal expertise, governance experience, and an understanding of innovation and economic opportunity.

Harman previously served as a Student Member of the Kwantlen Polytechnic University Board of Governors, representing more than 22,000 students. In this role, he gained valuable experience in institutional governance, strategic decision-making, accountability, and advocating for the interests of a diverse community.

He is currently completing his legal articling in British Columbia and holds a J.D./BBA LL.B. His education also includes public policy studies at the London School of Economics and Political Science, entrepreneurship studies at Babson College, and an advanced diploma in computer programming. This interdisciplinary background gives him a broad perspective on law, public policy, technology, and economic development.

Harman is committed to helping build safer, healthier, and more resilient communities across British Columbia. His priorities include safer neighbourhoods, stronger responses to homelessness, addiction, and mental-health challenges, improved access to justice, greater opportunities in education and skills development, and public institutions that are accessible, transparent, and accountable.

Outside of his professional life, Harman values family, fitness, and lifelong learning. He enjoys yoga and working out and especially cherishes time with his six-year-old niece and four-year-old nephew. They keep him grounded and remind him of the importance of building a better future for the next generation.

Harman speaks English, Punjabi, and Hindi, allowing him to connect with and listen to people from diverse backgrounds across Surrey-Newton. His experience in law, public policy, technology, business, and governance gives him a broad and practical perspective on the challenges facing our community.

He is committed to bringing that experience into public service – by carefully listening to residents, understanding the issues that matter most to families and businesses, and working toward practical solutions for a stronger, safer, and more prosperous Surrey-Newton and British Columbia.

Name: Harj Dhaliwal
Bio:
Dr. Harj Dhaliwal is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey-Newton.

He is a business executive, educator and community leader with extensive experience in organizational leadership, governance, public transportation and community development. Over the course of his career, he has held senior executive and leadership roles in both the private and post-secondary sectors. In business, he has led complex organizations and major construction development initiatives, working with diverse teams and stakeholders across British Columbia.

Dr. Dhaliwal holds an MBA and a PhD in Organization Development and Leadership. He has taught business and management courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels. He brings significant public-sector governance experience, having served six years as a Director of TransLink and four years on the board of the BC SPCA.

Dr. Dhaliwal has been a longtime leader in youth soccer in Newton and across the region. He has served as Chair of the South Fraser District Association, Chair of the Surrey Metro Soccer Association, Board Member of the BC Coastal Soccer League, and President of the Central City Breakers Football Club in Newton.

He has lived in Surrey for 28 years, where he and his wife raised their family, and has been an active community leader throughout that time.

Name: Jessie Sunner
Bio:
Standing up for Surrey-Newton

Having grown up in Surrey, Jessie knows firsthand what makes this community such a special place to live, work and raise a family. As the MLA for Surrey-Newton, Jessie spent her first term fighting for this community and making sure Surrey has a strong voice at the table. You can count on her to stand up for families in Surrey-Newton, and fight every day to protect the services that people count on from Conservative cuts.

As Minister of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills, Jessie worked to expand opportunities for students and apprentices, and ensure British Columbians are first in line for the jobs of the future. She has also fought to bring the investments Surrey deserves, including a new SFU Medical School, the Surrey-Langley SkyTrain extension, more than 15,000 new student spaces, and the infrastructure needed to support our growing community.

Before entering politics, Jessie was a labour and human rights lawyer and trade unionist, where she fought for everyday working people. She has brought that same determination to public life.

Where the BC Conservatives would roll over for Trump and cut the things people rely on, Jessie Sunner, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for BC, protect the services that matter to families, and build our economy.

The plan is working. And we can’t stop now.

Name: Bryan Tepper
Bio:
A Dedicated Community Advocate for Surrey-Panorama

Bryan Tepper has proudly called Surrey home for two decades, residing in Ocean Park with his wife Rona following a transfer to the Surrey Detachment of the RCMP. Immersing himself in the community, Bryan quickly realized he had found the greatest place to live in Canada.

Engaged Policing Career

Bryan has spent his career serving as an RCMP officer, with the last 10 years exclusively in Surrey. In his role, he intimately engaged with the community, understanding both its challenges and its unique greatness. From witnessing tragic events to sharing in the joy of community celebrations, his policing career deeply embedded him in the fabric of Surrey-Panorama.

Milestone Advocacy

As the treasurer of the Mounted Police Professional Association of Canada (MPPAC), Bryan played a crucial role in successfully taking the federal government to court, securing the right to associate for RCMP members. This landmark lawsuit paved the way for RCMP members to have representation, a significant achievement for the policing community.

Dedicated Community Involvement

Both Bryan and Rona are active volunteers in various community organizations, including the Ocean Park Community Association, Crescent Beach Property Owners Association, Crescent Beach Swim Club, Surrey Orcas Water Polo, and the Crescent Beach Yacht Club. Their love for the water extends to Rona, who serves as the station leader of the local marine search and rescue. Outside of the real world, Bryan volunteers at all three levels of government.

Priorities for Surrey-Panorama

Bryan’s priorities include working towards repairing the medical system, starting with the recruitment of healthcare heroes and expanding training within the province. While acknowledging there’s no quick fix, he emphasizes the need to take steps to reverse the damage done to the healthcare system. Additionally, Bryan envisions the development of our natural resources as the most sustainable, cleanest, and most ethical in the world. The revenue generated from such development, without roadblocks, would significantly contribute to the future of healthcare in the region.

Name: Nolen Scott
Bio:
Nolen Scott is a film professional, musician, labour organizer and community advocate with nearly a decade of experience working in British Columbia’s film and television industry.

As an Assistant Director, Nolen has worked on major productions including Shōgun , Tron: Ares and Off Campus , as well as independent Canadian productions including Sweet Summer Pow Wow . His experience in the industry has shaped his commitment to stronger labour protections, fair pay and better working conditions.

Nolen previously served for two terms on the Production Assistants Caucus Advisory Committee of the Directors Guild of Canada, where he advocated for increased rest periods, higher pay and other workplace improvements for production assistants.

Outside of film, Nolen is active in the Lower Mainland arts community. He is a co-founder and board member of the Vancouver Venue Co-op, an organization focused on supporting independent arts and culture. He helped organize the co-op’s first flagship festival, Everything But the Bagel , which supported more than 30 artists over a 20-hour event.

Nolen has also been involved in grassroots community organizing and has spent time speaking with residents about affordability, working conditions and the challenges facing families across the region. His work in both the film industry and music community has strengthened his commitment to workers, community participation and accessible arts and culture.

Nolen is running in Surrey-Panorama to advocate for working people and families, affordable housing, stronger communities and a government where residents feel their voices are heard.

Name: Jinny Sims
Bio:
Protecting what matters to families in Surrey-Panorama

Jinny Sims has spent her career working for people and building strong communities that are safe and inclusive for all.

Jinny was first elected as the MLA for Surrey-Panorama in 2017 and served as B.C.’s Minister of Citizens’ Services. She previously served as the Member of Parliament for Newton-North Delta from 2011 to 2015.

She is no stranger to standing up for people and fighting for the things that matter. As past president of the BC Teachers’ Federation, Jinny has been an advocate for children, families, and schools. And as a prominent radio talk show host, she has given voice to people in the community to speak about the issues that matter to them.

As an active community member, Jinny knows that while Surrey is a great place to live, it can be even better. She is committed to tackling extortion and organized crime, keeping our streets safe and giving young people the opportunities and support they need to stay away from gangs.

Jinny Sims, David Eby and the BC NDP are committed to standing up for working families, protecting good jobs and making life more affordable.

At a time when Donald Trump’s tariffs and threats are putting Canadian jobs and our economy at risk, you can count on Jinny to fight for Surrey families, defend B.C. workers and stand up for Canada.

Name: Jessy Sahota
Bio:
Jessy Sahota is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Surrey-Serpentine.

Jessy is a decorated law enforcement officer, international athlete, and dedicated community coach. In 2022, he was recognized by the International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP) as one of the world’s Top 40 Police Officers Under 40.

A multi-sport athlete, Jessy has earned national and international recognition in wrestling, jiu-jitsu, and kabaddi. While studying at Simon Fraser University, he won a national wrestling championship. Jessy is married to his high-school sweetheart, Ikjot Sandhu. Both are graduates of Tamanawis Secondary School.

Name: Sikander Kang
Bio:
Sikander Kang: Standing up for families in Surrey-Serpentine River

As a healthcare professional, Sikander Kang is ready to protect people and services and build a stronger economy for people in Surrey. He has established and manages five physiotherapy clinics in the Lower Mainland.

Sikander is deeply rooted in Surrey, combining clinical healthcare expertise with leadership in his community, including grassroots organizing with the BC NDP. His background in health helps him to connect authentically with people — reflecting a genuine commitment to public service, community building, and successful leadership.

He holds a Master's and a bachelor’s degree in Physiotherapy. He is married and he has two young children; one son and one daughter.

Sikander Kang, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for our province, to protect people and service, and to build a stronger economy - so that everyone can build a good life in the place they love.

Name: Waqas Rana
Bio:
Waqas Rana is a dedicated family man, community advocate, and professional running as the CentreBC candidate for Surrey-White Rock in the British Columbia provincial election.

At the heart of Rana’s life is his family. A proud local resident, he lives with his wife Dr. Alia, their three daughters Maha, Hiba and Zoya, son in law Rao Haider, a lively dog Gracie, a bird Sweety , and two cats Monster and Mongo. Balancing a busy household filled with school routines, activities, and daily family moments, Rana knows firsthand the everyday joys and pressures facing modern families, inspiring his deep personal commitment to building a stronger, safer future for the next generation.

Waqas’s public service is anchored by a solid academic background a CPA, CMA with a Bachelor and Master degree in Accounting and Finance and a proven professional track record in Financial Services. Over the course of his career in Banking and Insurance, he has led many key initiatives, projects and diverse teams, developing a reputation for sound fiscal judgment, rigorous problem-solving, and practical execution. He understands how economic decisions in Victoria directly impact local employers, workers, and household budgets.

Pairing this professional discipline with genuine community empathy, Waqas rejects partisan extremes to champion practical, balanced solutions that put everyday people first—from strengthening local healthcare capacity and tackling cost-of-living pressures to fostering responsible, family-friendly infrastructure and growth.

Above all, Waqas is dedicated to protecting the quality of life that makes Surrey-White Rock special, ensuring local residents are represented with compassion, integrity, and true accountability in Victoria.

Name: Trevor Halford
Bio:
Trevor Halford is a dedicated MLA for Surrey–White Rock, deeply rooted in the community where he was born and raised. Alongside his wife Holly, Trevor is raising their three young children in the same parks, fields, and rinks where he grew up, actively volunteering as a coach. His personal experiences with local challenges, such as housing affordability and commuting, drive his commitment to serving the needs of families in the Lower Mainland.

Career

Trevor Halford was first elected as MLA for Surrey–White Rock in 2020. He most recently served as the Shadow Minister for Transportation and Infrastructure, ICBC and Affordability, BC Transit, and Sport, having previously held roles as Shadow Minister for Mental Health and Addictions and Translink. A graduate of Elgin Park Secondary and Trinity Western University, Trevor’s career reflects his dedication to addressing local issues and advocating for a vibrant economy in Victoria.

Name: Christine Kinnie
Bio:
Christine currently works as a secondary school secretary, supporting students, families, educators and staff in a busy inner-city school. Through this work, she has seen firsthand how affordability, housing insecurity and access to essential services affect families and young people.

She returned to post-secondary education as a mature student and recently earned a Diploma in General Studies from Kwantlen Polytechnic University, graduating with a 4.15 GPA. She is continuing her education with the goal of attending law school and has a particular interest in human rights, constitutional law, Indigenous land rights and Canadian democracy.

Christine is also active in her community. She serves as a Lay Chaplain and Service Leader with the South Fraser Unitarians and has participated in community organizing, political events, fundraising and initiatives supporting local organizations.

In 2025, Christine ran as the Green Party of Canada candidate for South Surrey-White Rock in the federal election, gaining experience speaking with voters, listening to community concerns and participating in public advocacy.

Christine is passionate about democratic reform, proportional representation, economic fairness and environmental stewardship. She believes effective leadership starts with listening, treating people with respect and ensuring communities have a meaningful voice in the decisions that affect them.

Name: Deep Sandhu
Bio:
Deep Singh Sandhu is a seasoned businessman, longshoreman, and community engagement specialist with over two decades of leadership and entrepreneurial experience. With a strong background in forestry, real estate, and asset management, he has successfully led large-scale projects, driven business growth, and managed diverse teams across multiple sectors.

A long-time resident of Vancouver, BC for over 35 years, Deep is deeply committed to community service and fostering meaningful connections. Drawing from his fourth-generation

Canadian heritage, he is a recognized cultural ambassador between the Sikh community and the Tl’etinqox First Nations.

In this capacity, he has organized initiatives that unite youth in exploring and appreciating their shared cultures and histories.

Deep Singh is also a dedicated volunteer at Guru Nanak’s Free Kitchen, where he provides meals to Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside, and actively contributes to the Khalsa Diwan Society and other local community initiatives.

A former Reservist in the Canadian Armed Forces, Deep holds a Bachelor of Commerce in Finance and Marketing from the University of Northern British Columbia (UNBC). His passion

for mentoring young people is reflected in his previous role as a BC Field Hockey youth player representative, where he inspired youth to pursue excellence in athletics. He has organized various community events and sports tournaments to promote healthy lifestyles and community service.

Fluent in English, Punjabi, and Hindi, Deep has a strong personal interest in sports, nature, outdoor activities, reading and continuous learning. Deep resides in Vancouver with his wife, where they remain dedicated to both their professional endeavors and active community involvement.

Name: Françoise Raunet
Bio:
Françoise Raunet is a mother, public school teacher, union leader and lifelong Vancouverite who lives in a housing co-op in Vancouver-Fraserview. With more than 30 years of experience across education, publishing and community services, she has spent much of her career advocating for strong public schools, healthy communities and a more sustainable future.

Françoise is currently on leave from the classroom while serving as a Vice President of the Vancouver Elementary and Adult Educators Society. During her career with the Vancouver School Board, she has worked in a range of roles including School Support Worker, Resource Teacher, Late French Immersion teacher and District Curriculum Support Teacher.

Her experience also extends beyond the classroom. Françoise spent five years living and working in Taipei, Taiwan, where she worked in educational publishing. She holds a Bachelor of Education, a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology and a Master of Arts in International Studies with a focus on Complex Emergencies. She is fluent in French and also speaks some Spanish and Mandarin.

Françoise has spent decades advocating for healthy ecosystems, peace, electoral reform and economic reform. She previously ran as a BC Green candidate in Vancouver-Point Grey in 2011 and 2013, bringing her commitment to public education, climate action and democratic accountability into provincial politics.

As an educator and union leader, Françoise believes effective leadership means listening, bringing people together and working toward practical solutions. She is running in Vancouver-Fraserview to advocate for strong public services, environmental protection, economic fairness and a future where communities can thrive.

Name: Aman Singh
Bio:
Standing up for Vancouver-Fraserview.

Aman Singh is a prominent civil and human rights lawyer and served as MLA for Richmond-Queensborough from 2020-2024, making history as the first turban-wearing Sikh elected to the BC Legislature. Aman has appeared at the BC Provincial and Supreme Courts and the BC Court of Appeal. He is a socially-conscious small business owner and has held roles as a director of the Professor Mohan Singh Memorial Foundation, the Association of Legal Aid Lawyers, the Friends of the Sikh Cadets Society, the People’s Legal Education Society and as a Governor of Kwantlen Polytechnic University.

Aman was born in India, raised in Hong Kong, and moved with his family to B.C. Aman now lives in South Vancouver and takes pride and joy in being a father to his two children.

One of Aman’s missions is to bring more attention to the disease of addiction and the possibility of recovery. Aman is a recovered alcoholic who has been sober for over fifteen years and plays an active role in the recovery community. He has a deep understanding of the challenges faced by people and families who are dealing with addiction and believes that communities that foster care and respect for all are key to recovery.

Aman, David Eby, and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up for you, protect the services that you count on, and build for the future.

Name: Christian Bosio
Bio:
Christian Bosio is a global clean energy entrepreneur, engineer, and parent, and is focused on building practical solutions for British Columbia.

Driven by a commitment to the environment and with a degree in mechanical engineering, Christian launched his career in the clean hydrogen sector. After a decade in this industry, he co-founded a company in 2008, scaling it into an enterprise employing over 300 people and creating long-term economic value in the province. As an executive leader, he collaborated with global partners across diverse cultures, building a leadership style rooted in listening, trust, and collaboration. He will bring that same approach to his community in Vancouver-Hastings, one of the most diverse and vibrant communities in BC.

Christian is running with Centre BC to bring a socially liberal, fiscally responsible voice to BC politics, with a strong commitment to environmental sustainability. As a parent of two teenagers, he thinks about the province younger generations will inherit. He believes government needs to find the right balance: supporting the programs and services people rely on, growing the economy and creating good jobs, protecting the environment, and ensuring people can afford to build a life in the communities they call home.

Christian has spent his career finding common ground, bringing people together, and building practical solutions. He’s ready to bring that experience to BC politics.

Name: Phyllis Tang
Bio:
Phyllis Tang is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Vancouver-Hastings.

Born and raised in Vancouver, Phyllis lived in Vancouver-Hastings for more than 22 years.  Phyllis completed graduate studies in Ethnomusicology at UBC and in Toronto, earning the York University Graduate Scholarship for Academic Excellence, along with commerce courses in non-profit financial management, accounting and international finance. She has taught piano and music theory for more than 25 years and is fluent in English, Cantonese and Mandarin.

Phyllis has built a career in community outreach and public relations. She has worked as Alumni Relations Coordinator at UBC’s Sauder School of Business and Faculty of Education, Administrative Officer of the Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Garden Society, and Constituency Assistant to a Richmond-Queensborough MLA. She has worked on more than 18 political campaigns, served as Campaign Director for Richmond-Queensborough in the 2024 provincial election, and ran for Vancouver City Council in 2018.

Phyllis is running to fight for young people and families. She will advocate for more support for youth entrepreneurship and faster access to healthcare for British Columbians.

Name: Kyra Philbert
Bio:
Kyra Philbert (she/her) is an artist, scholar, and registered nurse with more than a decade of experience in healthcare. Her work is grounded in health equity, social justice, and the belief that urgent climate action is necessary to protect our collective well-being.

Kyra’s experiences as a nurse in Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside shaped her commitment to understanding and challenging the social conditions that contribute to poverty, inequity, and poor health. Seeing these realities firsthand led her to explore how systems, institutions, and public policy affect people’s ability to live healthy and dignified lives.

In 2022, Kyra completed a Bachelor of Arts in Gender, Race, Sexuality and Social Justice as well as a Master of Science in Nursing at the University of British Columbia. Her graduate research, Nurse Angélique , examined connections between the early colonial history of Canadian nursing and more than 400 years of Black history in Canada.

Drawing on the story of Marie-Joseph Angélique and the history of colonial institutions in Canada, Kyra’s scholarship asks difficult questions about power, oppression, criminalization, and whose experiences are recognized in our understanding of history. Her work reflects a commitment to examining the structures behind inequality and bringing perspectives that are often overlooked into public conversations.

Kyra brings together healthcare experience, academic research, and creative practice with a strong focus on the climate emergency. She believes addressing climate change requires the same urgency we bring to other threats to public health and that climate policy must also consider equity, justice, and the well-being of communities.

Name: Niki Sharma
Bio:
A champion for people in Vancouver-Hastings.

Niki has served as the MLA for Vancouver-Hastings since 2021. During her service, she has expanded local health care services, opened child care spaces and new schools.

Niki has also served as Deputy Premier and Attorney General with a strong record of taking on large corporations, including tech companies, fighting for online safety, expanding access to justice and transformed the justice system to better respond to sexual violence.

She has been honoured to serve the people of Vancouver-Hastings and would be honoured to continue.

Niki Sharma, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to stand up to Trump, lower costs, hire more healthcare workers, and make BC less dependent on the United States, so everyone can build a good life.

The plan is working. We can’t stop now.

Name: Aron Lageri
Bio:
Aron Lageri is the BC Conservative candidate for Vancouver-Kensington.

Aron brings more than 22 years of experience in health care to the Conservative team. He began his career as a medical imaging technologist at BC Children’s Hospital, caring for young patients and their families, and went on to hold senior leadership roles in the health sector, including as manager of the False Creek Surgical Centre.

Throughout his career, Aron has worked to strengthen the next generation of health care professionals, recruiting young people from local communities into health science programs. He has also served on the board of the Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists.

Aron holds a Bachelor of Science in Radiology and a postgraduate certificate in Long-Term Care Administration. He has volunteered with a range of community boards and organizations and knows first hand what it takes to deliver the timely, reliable health care British Columbians deserve.

Name: Mable Elmore
Bio:
Mable Elmore: Standing up for people in Vancouver-Kensington

Mable Elmore is deeply connected to the community in Vancouver-Kensington. Elected five times, Mable is the first and only member of the Legislative Assembly of BC who is of Filipino descent. In 2025, she assumed the concurrent role of Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, the first person of Asian heritage to take on this position.

Previously, in 2022, Premier David Eby appointed Mable as the Parliamentary Secretary for Anti-Racism Initiatives. Her work included striving to remove systemic barriers in government services for racialized and Indigenous peoples and beginning the engagement process for a future Filipino cultural centre.

As a member of David Eby’s BC NDP team, Mable is focused on standing up for British Columbia, protecting the services that people count on, and building for the future.

Name: Jaime Stein
Bio:
Jaime Stein is a business and non-profit executive, a former broadcast journalist, and the Conservative candidate in Vancouver-Langara. He is running on the issues British Columbians feel first: the cost of living, health care that is there when you need it, and safe streets in every neighbourhood. After years of NDP management that left the province with unsustainable debt and a shrinking economy, Jaime believes taxpayers deserve a return on every dollar and government should be judged on results.

Personal Life

Born and raised in Vancouver and a graduate of Point Grey Secondary School, Jaime lives in Vancouver with his wife Jessica and their three children. He has lived across Canada and worked around the world, and chose to raise his family in the city that raised him.

Health care is personal for Jaime. His father died of leukemia in 2006 after a search for a matching stem cell donor. In the years that followed, Jaime worked with Canadian Blood Services on the national campaign that raised $12.5 million to establish Canada’s first public cord blood bank, so that other families would not face the same odds. He has since served as Vice Chair of CLEAR (Canadians for Leading Edge Alzheimer’s Research), which funds Alzheimer’s and dementia research in British Columbia.

Professional Background

Jaime is Director for Western Canada at the Friends of Simon Wiesenthal Center, a national human rights organization, where he leads its education, advocacy and community engagement work across the West. He partners with police forces, health authorities, universities and governments, and delivers Holocaust education and antisemitism training to thousands of front-line professionals each year.

Before joining the non-profit sector, Jaime spent two decades in broadcasting and technology. He began his career in media, where he was the radio voice of the CFL’s Toronto Argonauts on AM640 and spent four seasons as the on-camera host for the league’s website. He then moved into technology, holding senior roles at Hootsuite, BroadbandTV, ICUC and Taplytics, where he helped build a Vancouver company into a global brand, advised Fortune 500 clients, and led engagements across 14 countries on four continents.

Jaime holds an MBA from the Rotman School of Management, where he was valedictorian, a Bachelor of Journalism from Toronto Metropolitan University, and studied political science at McGill University.

Community Involvement

Jaime chaired the public affairs subcommittee of the Jewish Federation of British Columbia’s community crisis response team, working directly with elected officials on community safety and security policy, and serves on the Federation’s grants and allocations committee. He sits on the advisory board of CJPAC, a national organization that encourages Canadians to get involved in the political process, and is a Wexner Heritage Fellow, one of 20 chosen to represent Vancouver in the North America-wide program.

In 2025 he received the King Charles III Coronation Medal for his contributions to Canadian society.

Name: John Atoyebi
Bio:
John K. Atoyebi is a lawyer, former judge, public-sector investigator and community leader whose career has spanned law, public service and grassroots community work in Canada and internationally.

Before immigrating to Canada, John served as a Magistrate and District Court Judge in Nigeria, working on civil and criminal cases and promoting restorative justice. After arriving in Canada, he rebuilt his career from the ground up, working in retail, traffic control and construction while completing the requirements to practise law in Canada. He is now a member of the Law Society of British Columbia and the Nova Scotia Barristers’ Society and practises as Principal Legal Counsel at Kebuiii Global Law Corporation.

John also spent more than two years as an Investigator with the Office of the Ombudsperson of British Columbia, examining complaints involving administrative fairness across more than 75 municipalities, regional districts and improvement districts. His work also included advising on whistleblower protections under the Public Interest Disclosure Act.

His commitment to public service extends deeply into the community. John serves on the City of Vancouver’s Persons with Disabilities Advisory Committee, previously served on the Vancouver Heritage Commission and is Secretary of the Vancouver General Hospital Thrift Store Board. He is also Executive Director of the BC Black Advocacy Society and has helped create opportunities for Black British Columbians to participate more fully in civic and democratic life.

John is also active in food security and agriculture. As President of the African-Canadian Agricultural Producers Cooperative and a director of the African-Canadian Farmers Society, he has helped support farmer training and the production of culturally important foods in British Columbia.

John holds an LL.B. and LL.M. in Common Law and a Master of Intellectual Property and Development Policy. He is also pursuing an LL.M. at UBC’s Allard School of Law, where his research focuses on recidivism among previously incarcerated Canadians. In 2026, he received a BC Achievement Foundation Community Award for his community service.

Having experienced firsthand the challenges of rebuilding a career as a newcomer, John understands the pressures of housing costs, affordability and systemic barriers. He is running in Vancouver-Langara to bring a service-oriented approach grounded in fairness, accountability, sustainability and dignity to the Legislature.

Name: Sunita Dhir
Bio:
Sunita Dhir: Standing up for people in Vancouver-Langara

Sunita Dhir was elected as the MLA for Vancouver-Langara in 2024, and she has called South Vancouver and Marpole home for three decades. Her commitment to her community began long before she entered public life: for nearly two decades, with SUCCESS, she supported newcomers in learning English and building lives in British Columbia.

In office, she has proudly served as the Parliamentary Secretary for International Credentials, working to make sure that internationally trained professionals have their skills and experience recognized so they can get a job in the field they've trained for and help build up BC’s economy.

Where the BC Conservatives would cozy up to Trump and gut services, you can count on Sunita to stand up for workers, families and newcomers in Vancouver-Langara. Sunita Dhir, David Eby and the BC NDP have a plan to protect what matters to people. It’s working. And we can’t stop now.

Name: Alex Muir
Bio:
Alexander Muir is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Vancouver-Little Mountain.

Born in Vancouver, Alexander grew up in Victoria and moved across the country as a child, living in Ottawa, Toronto and Edmonton before coming home to Vancouver to complete high school. As an athlete, Alexander represented Team BC in rugby, and earned his first cap for Canada’s U20 national team against Samoa at the 2025 Pacific Nations U20 Cup. After spending two years studying and playing rugby at University College Dublin, he returned home to Vancouver to finish his degree in political science at the University of British Columbia.

As a communications staffer in the Office of the Leader of the Official Opposition in Ottawa, he assisted in speech and press release writing and preparing Question Period materials on housing, forestry and resource issues. 

He believes a new generation of British Columbians deserves a province they can afford to build a life in and a government willing to fight for them.

Name: Christine Boyle
Bio:
Taking action for you in Vancouver-Little Mountain.

A strong advocate for rental, co-op and non-market housing, Christine was elected to Vancouver City Council in 2018 and re-elected in 2022. She has worked extensively in environmental and climate advocacy, including leading the development of Vancouver’s Climate Emergency Action Plan. An ordained United Church minister, and an enthusiastic cook and gardener, she lives in Vancouver with her husband and their two children.

Christine knows that the people of Vancouver-Little Mountain want a government that puts them first and prioritizes building more housing, improving healthcare and helping with costs.

Christine Boyle and David Eby are working hard every day to make sure we keep moving forward for people so everyone can build a good life here.

Name: Michael Davis
Bio:
Michael Davis is running in Vancouver-Point Grey because he believes government should manage the province’s finances responsibly and create the conditions for economic growth—so we can deliver strong healthcare, care for seniors and kids, and safe streets for all.

Michael recently retired as principal of a Vancouver communications and government relations firm. He served as Director of Communications for Canada’s Minister of Justice and Attorney General and has a long record as a community social impact leader. In 2021, his focus on climate action led him to launch Governance for Our Kids Climate.

Early in his career, Michael worked on tow-boats, drove taxi and a city bus, and shuttled rental planes—he holds a commercial pilot’s license.

An avid campaigner, Michael has worked at all three levels of government: constituency and nomination campaign manager federally, drafter of CentreBC’s bylaws, and manager of a City Council re-election and two mayoral campaigns municipally.

Michael holds a Master of Arts in Professional Communications from Royal Roads University.

He lives in Kitsilano with his partner and spends free time exploring BC’s back roads—and beyond—on an adventure motorcycle.

Name: Alex McMillan
Bio:
Alex McMillan is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Vancouver-Point Grey. 

Alex brings significant business experience to the Conservative Party of BC team. Most recently, he served as the CEO (Interim) of the British Columbia Chamber of Commerce, the largest and most broad-based business association in the province. In February, Alex returned to his own consultancy practice, which he started in 2020. 

Alex began his career as a senior political staffer and later as a civil servant in various provincial ministries in Victoria. After leaving government, he spent the next five years delivering consulting services to a broad range of clients at one of the country’s largest public relations firms. He then advised an integrated forestry company, responsible for the design and execution of their government relations strategies targeting the provincial government and over a dozen local municipalities where the company operated. With first-hand experience across many sectors and policy areas, Alex understands how to get the province building again. 

He and his wife live in Vancouver and have two teenage daughters. When not driving his children to their activities, Alex spends as much time on his bicycle as weather and work commitments will allow.

Name: Beatrice Sharpe
Bio:
Beatrice Sharpe (she/her) is a student, climate organizer, youth leader, entrepreneur, artist and author with five years of experience in political and environmental organizing. Her work focuses on affordability, climate action, social and ecological justice and creating opportunities for young people to participate in their communities.

Beatrice is currently studying Political Science and Environmental Studies at the University of Victoria, along with a certificate in Transformative Climate Action. As a full-time student working two jobs, she understands firsthand the pressures that housing costs, groceries and education expenses place on young people and renters.

Her organizing experience includes serving as Chair of the Young BC Greens, where she managed projects across the province ranging from wildfire restoration in Kelowna to public transit advocacy in Victoria. She currently chairs Green Nation Collective Changemakers, which provides financial support and mentorship to young entrepreneurs working to create positive change in their communities.

Beatrice has also worked as Canvass Director with the Ancient Forest Alliance, where she helped raise funds in support of old-growth forest protection. Her broader community involvement includes work with Ocean Wise and the City of Victoria Youth Council, contributing to more than 1,000 hours of community service.

As an artist and writer, Beatrice published A Message from Our Mother , a poetry collection exploring gender inequality, environmental degradation and humanity’s relationship with the natural world. She has also presented at the University of Victoria on Canada’s energy future.

Beatrice is running in Vancouver-Point Grey to bring the concerns of students, renters and young people into public decision-making, with a focus on affordable housing, healthcare, public education, renewable energy, public transit and climate action. She believes leadership requires listening, open discussion and meaningful communication with the people government represents.

Beatrice is a settler living, studying and working on the lands of the Lək̓ʷəŋən (Songhees and Xʷsepsəm/Esquimalt) Peoples.

Name: David Eby
Bio:
David Eby is a determined problem-solver, willing to stand up to powerful interests to get results for people.

From working in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside as a human rights lawyer to defending people as BC's 37th Premier, David Eby has spent his life standing up to powerful interests — and getting results.

David grew up in Kitchener, Ontario, the eldest of four siblings. His parents, Brian and Laura, strongly believed in the importance of fairness, and taught that value to their kids. David took it to heart from a young age.

After completing high school (where he was elected student council president) and an undergraduate degree at the University of Waterloo, David began his studies at the Schulich School of Law at Dalhousie University.

He quickly co-founded a group to promote equality called SALSA — the Social Activist Law Student Association, which still exists today.

After finishing law school, David wanted to work where he could do the most good for people. So, in 2005, he started working in Canada's most diverse — and poorest — postal code: Vancouver's Downtown Eastside.

As he worked to protect British Columbians dealing with a growing housing crisis, David saw big problems that needed to be fixed for people — that right wing politicians were refusing to deal with them.

In 2011 David took on a new challenge so he could help more people: running against BC Liberal Premier, Christy Clark, in her riding of Vancouver Point-Grey, which had long voted for her party and its candidates.

David knocked on hundreds of doors and made thousands of calls, and listened to the people of the riding who felt like they had been neglected by the BC Liberals. A huge criticism of Christy Clark at the time was that she was never around. Her office was usually closed, she didn’t come to events in the community, and she never had time for people.

Right from the start, David did things differently. He connected with people and worked to understand their problems, so they could find solutions together.

Come election day, David made history — and has represented the people of Vancouver-Point Grey ever since.

Over the next four years, David worked hard for people to uncover and expose the entitlement and excess of the BC Liberals. He fought against the choices they made for their big money donors and how they hurt British Columbians.

When John Horgan became Premier in 2017, David became BC’s Attorney General to take on some of the worst ways BC Liberal policies favoured those at the top.

John put him in charge of some of the province’s most difficult challenges — extinguishing the BC Liberal ‘dumpster fire’ at ICBC and fighting criminal money laundering that inflated BC housing prices out of reach, and fueled the toxic drug crisis.

David rolled up his sleeves and got to work.

As the longest-serving Attorney General in the last 30 years, David delivered results for people.

He turned around ICBC’s finances and reduced the average driver’s car insurance rates by 20%. He led a successful crackdown on money laundering in casinos. He took on opioid manufacturers and delivered a first of its kind settlement to hold corporations accountable for the overdose crisis — the largest health cost recovery in Canadian history. The first bill he introduced in the legislature banned big money from provincial politics.

David became Minister of Housing in 2020 and started implementing creative solutions to tackle the housing crisis.

In the year and a half he led the ministry, he helped build thousands of homes all over the province and brought almost 5,000 people off the street and into housing.

On November 18, 2022, David became BC’s 37th premier, launching a 100 Days of Action plan to help people build a good life here.

On his first day he announced cost-of-living relief for BC Hydro ratepayers, and got to work taking on the big causes of inequality and the housing crisis.

In his first eighteen months as Premier, David Eby has taken bold action for people.

To tackle the housing crisis, he and our BC NDP team have brought in tough new rules regulating short-term rentals to turn them into homes for people, along with updating zoning rules province-wide to allow for more townhouses, duplexes and triplexes. He's also introduced new initiatives to help renters, improve health care by hiring more doctors and nurses, and passed new laws to help keep communities and people safe. And there's so much more to do.

Through all of this, David remains a dedicated father, husband, pillow fort engineer and dad joke connoisseur.

He and his wife Cailey, a family doctor, welcomed their son Ezra in 2014 and their daughter Iva in 2019. They welcomed their third daughter, Gwendolyn, in June 2024.

Name: Petra Kuret
Bio:
Petra Kuret brings leadership experience, energy, and commitment to Vancouver-Quilchena, her home for more than 40 years and where she raised her family. Petra is running because our children deserve a future, not a bill. She’ll bring fiscal discipline, economic growth, and a commitment to respectful dialogue to the Legislature.

Petra brings more than 35 years of results-driven leadership across government, business, social impact, and artificial intelligence. She was honoured to start her career as a Parliamentary Page in the House of Commons and worked for Members of Parliament in Canada and the UK. In 2025, she sought the Federal Liberal nomination in Vancouver Quadra.

In 1993, Petra joined Accenture and led large-scale technology projects, business transformations, and mergers in the critical resource industries in North America. In 2012, she became Managing Partner for British Columbia and set a bold vision of growth and led a highly engaged 1000+ workforce.

Seeking to make a greater impact closer to home, Petra served as Senior Vice President of Strategy and Transformation at VANCITY Credit Union focused on growing the business and using finance as a tool for social impact.

In 2021, she joined a Silicon Valley AI B-Corp working with Fortune 500 companies to upskill and reskill workforces through ethical AI. The World Economic Forum named the company a Technology Pioneer that same year.

Petra was recognized as a Top 100 Most Powerful Women in Canada in 2016 and 2017. In 2025, she was humbled to receive the King Charles III Coronation Medal for her community service. She is a dedicated community builder and Board member with organizations like Mosaic (Board Chair), BC Women’s Hospital, and others. Her passion project has been securing provincial funding to build a new 178-bed long term care home with an innovative model of care for seniors.

Petra holds an Honours BA in Political Science from Carleton University, studied at Université en France and the University of Leeds, and holds the ICD.D and GCB.D governance designations.

Petra lives in Dunbar with her husband John, son and daughter, and corgi Ember. Petra is ready to listen, connect, and turn shared ideas into lasting impact.

Name: Carson Binda
Bio:
Carson Binda is the Conservative Party of BC candidate for Vancouver-Quilchena.

Carson was the B.C. Director of the Canadian Taxpayers Federation, where he advocated for lower taxes, accountable government and responsible public spending. He regularly appears in provincial and national media and has written extensively on B.C. politics, taxation and government accountability.

Before joining the CTF in 2022, Carson worked in senior roles on political campaigns at the municipal, provincial and federal levels while studying at the University of British Columbia. He served as a logistics officer in the Canadian army reserves.

Carson spent much of his childhood and adolescence living abroad, including in Yemen, Kosovo, Nigeria and Malta. Those experiences gave him an early interest in government, public institutions and the impact political decisions can have on people’s everyday lives.

Carson lives in Vancouver with his fiancée and their Bernese Mountain Dog. Outside of work, he can usually be found hiking and scrambling in the mountains of British Columbia.

Name: Douglas Courtemanche
Bio:
Dr. Douglas Courtemanche is a semi-retired craniofacial surgeon, clinical professor and health researcher with more than 35 years of experience caring for patients in British Columbia’s healthcare system.

Douglas grew up in Vancouver-Quilchena, where he went to school, played road hockey and developed a lifelong love of the outdoors through hiking, camping and sailing. He later attended medical school at the University of British Columbia and trained as a plastic surgeon specializing in craniofacial surgery.

Over the course of his career, Douglas has cared for children with complex medical needs, advocated for patients and supported colleagues across the healthcare system. He has also served in leadership roles including President of the BC Medical Association’s Section of Plastic Surgery and Medical Staff President at BC Children’s and Women’s Hospital.

Douglas has been a Clinical Professor in UBC’s Department of Surgery since 2008 and has contributed to more than 80 publications. He also conducts clinical research as an investigator with the BC Children’s Research Institute.

A major focus of his recent work has been the relationship between human health and the environment. He has taught medical students and practising physicians about the impacts of climate change and pollution on human and planetary health, and in 2025 received the Planetary Health Award from the Canadian Society of Plastic Surgeons.

Douglas is running in Vancouver-Quilchena to bring his experience in healthcare, teaching, research and patient advocacy to public service, with a focus on supporting healthier people, stronger communities and a healthier planet.

Name: Callista Ryan
Bio:
Callista Ryan: building up Vancouver-Quilchena

Callista Ryan is a communications professional who has worked across the public service, non-profit and private sectors.

She has worked with the BC Public Service on communications and engagement for programs supporting young people and families.
